4.24.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca ..
nigūḍhaṃ śṛṇu vṛttāntaṃ munerdurvāsaso mune ..
aho'sya dārasaṃyogaḥ kathaṃ tadūrdhvaretasaḥ .. 1 ..
4.24.d:
नारायण उवाच ॥
निगूढं शृणु वृत्तान्तं मुनेर्दुर्वाससो मुने ॥
अहोऽस्य दारसंयोगः कथं तदूर्ध्वरेतसः ॥ 1 ॥

4.24.s:
dṛṣṭvā tayośca śṛṅgāraṃ muniḥ kāmī babhūva ha ..
jitendriyo'satsaṃsargāddoṣaḥ sāṃsargiko bhavet .. 2 ..
4.24.d:
दृष्ट्वा तयोश्च शृङ्गारं मुनिः कामी बभूव ह ॥
जितेन्द्रियोऽसत्संसर्गाद्दोषः सांसर्गिको भवेत् ॥ 2 ॥

4.24.s:
sahasā tasya hṛdaye babhūva surate spṛhā ..
tapastaptvā tatra dadhyau kāminīṃ madanāturaḥ .. 3 ..
4.24.d:
सहसा तस्य हृदये बभूव सुरते स्पृहा ॥
तपस्तप्त्वा तत्र दध्यौ कामिनीं मदनातुरः ॥ 3 ॥

4.24.s:
etasminnantare tena pathā yāti munīśvaraḥ ..
prārthayantyā patiṃ santamaurvaśca sutayā saha .. 4 ..
4.24.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तेन पथा याति मुनीश्वरः ॥
प्रार्थयन्त्या पतिं सन्तमौर्वश्च सुतया सह ॥ 4 ॥

4.24.s:
ūrūdbhavo brahmaṇaśca purā kalpe tapasyataḥ ..
ūrdhvaretāśca yogīndra orvastena iti smṛtaḥ .. 5 ..
4.24.d:
ऊरूद्भवो ब्रह्मणश्च पुरा कल्पे तपस्यतः ॥
ऊर्ध्वरेताश्च योगीन्द्र ओर्वस्तेन इति स्मृतः ॥ 5 ॥

4.24.s:
tasya jānūdbhavā kanyā kandalī nāma viśrutā ..
durvāsasaṃ prārthayantī nānyaṃ manasi rocate .. 6 ..
4.24.d:
तस्य जानूद्भवा कन्या कन्दली नाम विश्रुता ॥
दुर्वाससं प्रार्थयन्ती नान्यं मनसि रोचते ॥ 6 ॥

4.24.s:
sasuto hi muniśreṣṭho munerdurvāsasaḥ puraḥ ..
tasthau mahāprasannaśca jvaladagniśikhopamaḥ .. .. 7 ..
4.24.d:
ससुतो हि मुनिश्रेष्ठो मुनेर्दुर्वाससः पुरः ॥
तस्थौ महाप्रसन्नश्च ज्वलदग्निशिखोपमः ॥ ॥ 7 ॥

4.24.s:
munīndro'pi munīndraṃ taṃ puro dṛṣṭvā sasaṃbhramaḥ ..
prajavena samuttasthau nanāma ca mudā'nvitaḥ ..8..
4.24.d:
मुनीन्द्रोऽपि मुनीन्द्रं तं पुरो दृष्ट्वा ससंभ्रमः ॥
प्रजवेन समुत्तस्थौ ननाम च मुदाऽन्वितः ॥8॥

4.24.s:
aurvo durvāsasaṃ tatra samāśliṣya mudā'nvitaḥ ..
uvāca munaye sarvaṃ kanyakāyā manoratham .. 9 ..
4.24.d:
और्वो दुर्वाससं तत्र समाश्लिष्य मुदाऽन्वितः ॥
उवाच मुनये सर्वं कन्यकाया मनोरथम् ॥ 9 ॥

4.24.s:
aurva uvāca ..
vikhyātā kandalī nāma mama kanyā manoharā ..
prauḍhā tvāmeva dhyāyantī śrutvā vācikavaktrataḥ .. 4.24.10 ..
4.24.d:
और्व उवाच ॥
विख्याता कन्दली नाम मम कन्या मनोहरा ॥
प्रौढा त्वामेव ध्यायन्ती श्रुत्वा वाचिकवक्त्रतः ॥ 4.24.10 ॥

4.24.s:
ayonisambhavā kanyā trailokyaṃ mohituṃ kṣamā ..
sarvarūpaguṇādhārā doṣeṇaikena saṃyutā .. 11 ..
4.24.d:
अयोनिसम्भवा कन्या त्रैलोक्यं मोहितुं क्षमा ॥
सर्वरूपगुणाधारा दोषेणैकेन संयुता ॥ 11 ॥

4.24.s:
atīva kalahāviṣṭā kopena kaṭubhāṣiṇī ..
nānāguṇayutaṃ dravyaṃ na tyajedekadoṣataḥ .. 12 ..
4.24.d:
अतीव कलहाविष्टा कोपेन कटुभाषिणी ॥
नानागुणयुतं द्रव्यं न त्यजेदेकदोषतः ॥ 12 ॥

4.24.s:
aurvasya vacanaṃ śrutvā harṣaśokānvito muniḥ ..
dadarśa kanyāṃ purato guṇarūpasamanvitām .. 13 ..
4.24.d:
और्वस्य वचनं श्रुत्वा हर्षशोकान्वितो मुनिः ॥
ददर्श कन्यां पुरतो गुणरूपसमन्विताम् ॥ 13 ॥

4.24.s:
śaratpārvaṇacandrāsyāṃ śaratpaṅkajalocanām ..
īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyāṃ pīnaśroṇipayodharām .. 14 ..
4.24.d:
शरत्पार्वणचन्द्रास्यां शरत्पङ्कजलोचनाम् ॥
ईषद्धास्यप्रसन्नास्यां पीनश्रोणिपयोधराम् ॥ 14 ॥

4.24.s:
navayauvanasaṃyuktāṃ paśyantīṃ vakracakṣuṣā ..
ratnālaṃkāraśobhāḍhyāṃ vahniśuddhāṃśukānvitām .. 15 ..
4.24.d:
नवयौवनसंयुक्तां पश्यन्तीं वक्रचक्षुषा ॥
रत्नालंकारशोभाढ्यां वह्निशुद्धांशुकान्विताम् ॥ 15 ॥

4.24.s:
munirmumoha tāṃ dṛṣṭvā kāmabāṇaprapīḍitaḥ ..
uvāca taṃ muniśreṣṭhaṃ hṛdayena vidūyatā .. 16 ..
4.24.d:
मुनिर्मुमोह तां दृष्ट्वा कामबाणप्रपीडितः ॥
उवाच तं मुनिश्रेष्ठं हृदयेन विदूयता ॥ 16 ॥

4.24.s:
durvāsā uvāca ..
nārīrūpaṃ tribhuvane muktimārganirodhakam ..
vyavadhānaṃ tapasyāyāḥ satataṃ mohakāraṇam .. 17 ..
4.24.d:
दुर्वासा उवाच ॥
नारीरूपं त्रिभुवने मुक्तिमार्गनिरोधकम् ॥
व्यवधानं तपस्यायाः सततं मोहकारणम् ॥ 17 ॥

4.24.s:
kārāgāre ca saṃsāre durvahaṃ nigaḍaṃ param ..
acchedyaṃ jñānakhaḍgaiśca mahadbhiḥ śaṃkarādibhiḥ .. 18 ..
4.24.d:
कारागारे च संसारे दुर्वहं निगडं परम् ॥
अच्छेद्यं ज्ञानखड्गैश्च महद्भिः शंकरादिभिः ॥ 18 ॥

4.24.s:
saṅgicchāyātiriktaṃ ca karmabhogātparātparam ..
indriyādindriyādhārādvidyāyāśca materapi .. 19..
4.24.d:
सङ्गिच्छायातिरिक्तं च कर्मभोगात्परात्परम् ॥
इन्द्रियादिन्द्रियाधाराद्विद्यायाश्च मतेरपि ॥ 19॥
4.24.m:
It persists beyond a companion and a shadow, beyond the experience of action,
beyond the sense-organs, the seat of the senses, learning, and the intellect. // 19

4.24.s:
ādehaṃ saṅginī chāyā bhogāntaṃ bhoga eva ca ..
dehendriyāṇi jīvāntaṃ vidyā caivāvaśīlinam .. 4.24.20 ..
4.24.d:
आदेहं सङ्गिनी छाया भोगान्तं भोग एव च ॥
देहेन्द्रियाणि जीवान्तं विद्या चैवावशीलिनम् ॥ 4.24.20 ॥
4.24.m:
A companion is a shadow until the body [perishes], and experience lasts only until the end of [that] experience;
the body and sense organs last until the end of life, and knowledge belongs only to the disciplined one. // 4.24.20

4.24.s:
matiścaivāvaśīlāntā sukhī janmanijanmani ..
yāvajjīvī ca sustrīko na tāvajjanmakhaṇḍanam ..21 ..
4.24.d:
मतिश्चैवावशीलान्ता सुखी जन्मनिजन्मनि ॥
यावज्जीवी च सुस्त्रीको न तावज्जन्मखण्डनम् ॥21 ॥
4.24.m:
And the mind lasts until lack of conduct ends; [such a person] is happy birth after birth.
As long as one has a good wife throughout life, there is no termination of [happy] birth. // 21

4.24.s:
yāvacca jīvino janma tāvadbhogaḥ sukhāvahaḥ ..
paraṃ munīndra sarvasmāddharipādābjasevanam.. 22 ..
4.24.d:
यावच्च जीविनो जन्म तावद्भोगः सुखावहः ॥
परं मुनीन्द्र सर्वस्माद्धरिपादाब्जसेवनम्॥ 22 ॥
4.24.m:
As long as a living being has birth, so long does enjoyment bring happiness;
yet above all, O king of sages, is service to Hari's lotus feet. // 22

4.24.s:
dhyāyataḥ kṛṣṇapādābjaṃ mama vighno babhūva ha ..
na jāne karmadoṣeṇa kena vā pūrvajanmanaḥ .. 23 ..
4.24.d:
ध्यायतः कृष्णपादाब्जं मम विघ्नो बभूव ह ॥
न जाने कर्मदोषेण केन वा पूर्वजन्मनः ॥ 23 ॥
4.24.m:
While I was meditating on Kṛṣṇa's lotus feet, an obstacle arose indeed—
I know not by what fault of actions from a previous birth! // 23

4.24.s:
puṃścalyā saha śṛṅgāraṃ dṛṣṭvā daityasya manmanaḥ ..
babhūva kāmasaṃyuktaṃ dattaṃ dhātrā ca tatphalam ..24..
4.24.d:
पुंश्चल्या सह शृङ्गारं दृष्ट्वा दैत्यस्य मन्मनः ॥
बभूव कामसंयुक्तं दत्तं धात्रा च तत्फलम् ॥24॥
4.24.m:
Having seen a Daitya's lovemaking with an unchaste woman, my mind
became possessed by desire, and the Creator granted the fruit of that. // 24

4.24.s:
kiṃ tvahaṃ tava kanyāyāḥ kaṭūktiśatakaṃ mune ..
dhruvaṃ kṣamāṃ kariṣyāmi dāsyāmi ca tataḥ phalam ..25..
4.24.d:
किं त्वहं तव कन्यायाः कटूक्तिशतकं मुने ॥
ध्रुवं क्षमां करिष्यामि दास्यामि च ततः फलम् ॥25॥
4.24.m:
However, O sage, up to a hundred harsh words from your daughter
I will certainly forgive, and after that I will inflict the consequence. // 25

4.24.s:
sarvato'pi parā nindā strīkaṭūktisahiṣṇutā ..
atīva ninditaḥ satsu strījito bhuvanatraye .. 25 ..
4.24.d:
सर्वतोऽपि परा निन्दा स्त्रीकटूक्तिसहिष्णुता ॥
अतीव निन्दितः सत्सु स्त्रीजितो भुवनत्रये ॥ 25 ॥
4.24.m:
Above all else, enduring harsh words from a woman is great disgrace;
one who is subdued by a woman is exceedingly despised among the virtuous in the three worlds. // 26

4.24.s:
tavājñāṃ mastake kṛtvā grahīṣyāmi sutāṃ tava ..
upetāṃ kāminīṃ tyaktvā kālasūtraṃ vrajennaraḥ ..27..
4.24.d:
तवाज्ञां मस्तके कृत्वा ग्रहीष्यामि सुतां तव ॥
उपेतां कामिनीं त्यक्त्वा कालसूत्रं व्रजेन्नरः ॥27॥
4.24.m:
Placing your command upon my head, I shall take your daughter.
A man who abandons a passionate woman who has approached him would go to Kālasūtra. // 27

4.24.s:
rahasyupasthitāṃ kāmātpuṃścalīṃ cejjitendriyaḥ ..
parityajeddharmabhayādadharmānnarakaṃ vrajet .. 28 ..
4.24.d:
रहस्युपस्थितां कामात्पुंश्चलीं चेज्जितेन्द्रियः ॥
परित्यजेद्धर्मभयादधर्मान्नरकं व्रजेत् ॥ 28 ॥
4.24.m:
If a man of controlled senses should abandon, out of fear of dharma,
an unchaste woman who presents herself in secret out of lust, he would go to hell through unrighteousness. // 28

4.24.s:
ityevamuktvā durvāsā virarāma muneḥ puraḥ ..
munirvedoktavidhinā dadau tasmai sutāṃ mune .. 29 ..
4.24.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा दुर्वासा विरराम मुनेः पुरः ॥
मुनिर्वेदोक्तविधिना ददौ तस्मै सुतां मुने ॥ 29 ॥
4.24.m:
Having spoken thus, Durvāsas paused before the sage.
The sage gave him his daughter according to the Vedic rite, O sage. // 29

4.24.s:
svastītyuvāca durvāsā muniśca yautukaṃ dadau ..
kanyāsamarpaṇaṃ kṛtvā mohāccaiva ruroda ha .. 4.24.30 ..
4.24.d:
स्वस्तीत्युवाच दुर्वासा मुनिश्च यौतुकं ददौ ॥
कन्यासमर्पणं कृत्वा मोहाच्चैव रुरोद ह ॥ 4.24.30 ॥
4.24.m:
Durvāsas said, “Svasti!” and the sage gave a dowry.
Having handed over his daughter, he wept out of attachment. // 30

4.24.s:
mūrcchāmavāpa sa muniḥ svakanyāvirahāturaḥ ..
apatyabhedaśokaughaḥ svātmārāmaṃ na muñcati .. 31 ..
4.24.d:
मूर्च्छामवाप स मुनिः स्वकन्याविरहातुरः ॥
अपत्यभेदशोकौघः स्वात्मारामं न मुञ्चति ॥ 31 ॥
4.24.m:
That sage fainted, afflicted with the pain of separation from his daughter.
The flood of grief born of separation from one's child does not spare even one who delights in the self. // 31

4.24.s:
kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya bodhayāmāsa kanyakām ..
mūrcchitāṃ tātavicchedādrudantīṃ śokasaṃyutām .. 32 ..
4.24.d:
क्षणेन चेतनां प्राप्य बोधयामास कन्यकाम् ॥
मूर्च्छितां तातविच्छेदाद्रुदन्तीं शोकसंयुताम् ॥ 32 ॥
4.24.m:
Regaining consciousness in a moment, he consoled the maiden,
who had fainted from separation from her father, weeping and filled with sorrow. // 32

4.24.s:
aurva uvāca ..
śṛṇu vatse pravakṣyāmi nītisāraṃ sudurlabham ..
hitaṃ satyaṃ ca vedoktaṃ pariṇāmasukhāvaham ..33..
4.24.d:
और्व उवाच ॥
शृणु वत्से प्रवक्ष्यामि नीतिसारं सुदुर्लभम् ॥
हितं सत्यं च वेदोक्तं परिणामसुखावहम् ॥33॥
4.24.m:
Listen, my child, I shall declare the essence of conduct, very hard to obtain,
beneficial, true, taught in the Vedas, and bringing happiness in the end. // 33

4.24.s:
svakāntaśca paro bandhuriha loke paratra ca ..
na hi kāntātparaḥ preyān kulastrīṇāṃ paro guruḥ ..34..
4.24.d:
स्वकान्तश्च परो बन्धुरिह लोके परत्र च ॥
न हि कान्तात्परः प्रेयान् कुलस्त्रीणां परो गुरुः ॥34॥
4.24.m:
One's husband is the supreme relative in this world and in the next;
there is none dearer than the husband, no higher guru for women of noble family. // 34

4.24.s:
devapūjā vrataṃ dānaṃ tapaścānaśanaṃ japaḥ ..
snānaṃ ca sarvatīrtheṣu dīkṣā sarvamakheṣu ca ..35..
4.24.d:
देवपूजा व्रतं दानं तपश्चानशनं जपः ॥
स्नानं च सर्वतीर्थेषु दीक्षा सर्वमखेषु च ॥35॥
4.24.m:
Worship of the gods, vows, giving gifts, austerity, fasting, recitation of mantras,
bathing at all sacred shrines, and initiation into all sacrifices, // 35

4.24.s:
prādakṣiṇyaṃ pṛthivyāśca brāhmaṇātithisevanam ..
sarvāṇi patisevāyāḥ kalāṃ nārhanti ṣoḍaśīm ..36..
4.24.d:
प्रादक्षिण्यं पृथिव्याश्च ब्राह्मणातिथिसेवनम् ॥
सर्वाणि पतिसेवायाः कलां नार्हन्ति षोडशीम् ॥36॥
4.24.m:
circumambulation of the earth, and service to brāhmaṇas and guests—
all these are not worth a sixteenth part of service to the husband. // 36

4.24.s:
kimetaiḥ patibhaktāyā abhaktāyāśca bhārate..
yadā duḥkhī sukhārambhe sākāṅkṣaḥ prathamo bhavet ..
patisevā paro dharmaḥ sarvaśāstreṣu paṭhyate..37..
4.24.d:
किमेतैः पतिभक्ताया अभक्तायाश्च भारते॥
यदा दुःखी सुखारम्भे साकाङ्क्षः प्रथमो भवेत् ॥
पतिसेवा परो धर्मः सर्वशास्त्रेषु पठ्यते॥37॥
4.24.m:
What use are these in Bhārata to a woman devoted to her husband, or to one not devoted?
When one is sorrowful at the onset of joy, eager at the outset—
service to the husband is proclaimed in all scriptures as the supreme dharma. // 37

4.24.s:
svaprajñānena satataṃ kāntaṃ nārāyaṇādhikam ..
dṛṣṭvā taccaraṇatmbhojasevāṃ nityaṃ kariṣyati.. .. 38 ..
4.24.d:
स्वप्रज्ञानेन सततं कान्तं नारायणाधिकम् ॥
दृष्ट्वा तच्चरणत्म्भोजसेवां नित्यं करिष्यति॥ ॥ 38 ॥
4.24.m:
Constantly seeing the husband through her own discernment as greater than Nārāyaṇa,
she must always render service to his lotus feet. // 38

4.24.s:
parihāsena kopena bhrameṇāvajñayā mune ..
kaṭūktiṃ svāminaḥ sākṣātparokṣānna kariṣyati .. 39 ..
4.24.d:
परिहासेन कोपेन भ्रमेणावज्ञया मुने ॥
कटूक्तिं स्वामिनः साक्षात्परोक्षान्न करिष्यति ॥ 39 ॥
4.24.m:
Neither in jest, nor in anger, nor in delusion, nor in contempt, O sage,
shall she utter a harsh word to her husband, whether directly or behind his back. // 39

4.24.s:
striyā vāgyoniduṣṭāyāḥ kāmato bhārate bhuvi ..
prāyaścittaṃ śrutau nāsti narakaṃ brahmaṇaḥ śatam ..4.24.40..
4.24.d:
स्त्रिया वाग्योनिदुष्टायाः कामतो भारते भुवि ॥
प्रायश्चित्तं श्रुतौ नास्ति नरकं ब्रह्मणः शतम् ॥4.24.40॥
4.24.m:
For a woman who is corrupt in speech or womb willfully on the soil of Bhārata,
there is no expiation in the Veda; [her fate is] hell for a hundred lifetimes of Brahmā. // 40

4.24.s:
sarvadharmaparītā yā kaṭūktiṃ kurute patim ..
śatajanmakṛtaṃ puṇyaṃ tasyā naśyati niścitam .. 41 ..
4.24.d:
सर्वधर्मपरीता या कटूक्तिं कुरुते पतिम् ॥
शतजन्मकृतं पुण्यं तस्या नश्यति निश्चितम् ॥ 41 ॥
4.24.m:
She who, though possessed of all virtues, speaks harsh words to her husband—
her merit acquired over a hundred lifetimes is surely destroyed. // 41

4.24.s:
dattvā kanyāṃ bodhayitvā jagāma munipuṃgavaḥ ..
svātmārāmaḥ svāśrame ca tasthau strīsahito mudā .. 42 ..
4.24.d:
दत्त्वा कन्यां बोधयित्वा जगाम मुनिपुंगवः ॥
स्वात्मारामः स्वाश्रमे च तस्थौ स्त्रीसहितो मुदा ॥ 42 ॥
4.24.m:
Having given away his daughter and instructed her, that eminent sage departed.
And he who delights in the self stayed in his hermitage joyfully with his wife. // 42

4.24.s:
sambhogecchāvṛte citte kāmī saṃprāpa kāminīm ..
aho sukṛtināṃ kāmo vāñchāmātreṇa sidhyati .. 43 ..
4.24.d:
सम्भोगेच्छावृते चित्ते कामी संप्राप कामिनीम् ॥
अहो सुकृतिनां कामो वाञ्छामात्रेण सिध्यति ॥ 43 ॥
4.24.m:
His heart overcome by the desire for sexual union, the lover obtained the lovely woman;
ah, the desire of the virtuous is accomplished by mere wishing! // 43

4.24.s:
śayyāṃ ratikarīṃ kṛtvā muniśreṣṭho mahāmune..
śubhe kṣaṇe gṛhītvā tāṃ suṣvāpa nirjane priyām..44..
4.24.d:
शय्यां रतिकरीं कृत्वा मुनिश्रेष्ठो महामुने॥
शुभे क्षणे गृहीत्वा तां सुष्वाप निर्जने प्रियाम्॥44॥
4.24.m:
Having prepared a bed conducive to love, the best of sages, O great sage,
taking his beloved at an auspicious moment, slept [with her] in solitude. // 44

4.24.s:
nārīrasānabhijñaḥ syādājanma munipuṃgavaḥ..
tathā'pi suratau vijñaḥ kāmaśāstraviśāradaḥ ..45..
4.24.d:
नारीरसानभिज्ञः स्यादाजन्म मुनिपुंगवः॥
तथाऽपि सुरतौ विज्ञः कामशास्त्रविशारदः ॥45॥
4.24.m:
Though the eminent sage had been ignorant of womanly pleasure since birth,
yet he was skilled in lovemaking, an expert in the science of love. // 45

4.24.s:
nānāprakāraṃ śṛṅgāraṃ cakāra vidhipūrvakam..
navasaṃgamamātreṇa mūrcchāṃ saṃprāpa kandalī .. 46 ..
4.24.d:
नानाप्रकारं शृङ्गारं चकार विधिपूर्वकम्॥
नवसंगममात्रेण मूर्च्छां संप्राप कन्दली ॥ 46 ॥
4.24.m:
He made love in various ways according to the proper rules.
From the mere first union, Kandalī fell into a swoon. // 46

4.24.s:
mūrcchāṃ prāpa muniśreṣṭho bubudhe na divāniśam ..
evaṃ pratidinaṃ tatra cakāra suratiṃ mune ..47 ..
4.24.d:
मूर्च्छां प्राप मुनिश्रेष्ठो बुबुधे न दिवानिशम् ॥
एवं प्रतिदिनं तत्र चकार सुरतिं मुने ॥47 ॥
4.24.m:
The best of sages too fell into a swoon and knew neither day nor night.
In this manner he engaged in lovemaking there every day, O sage. // 47

4.24.s:
vidagdhāyā vidagdhena babhūva saṃgamaḥ samaḥ ..
saṃbabhūva gṛhāsaktastapastyaktvā munīśvaraḥ .. 48 ..
4.24.d:
विदग्धाया विदग्धेन बभूव संगमः समः ॥
संबभूव गृहासक्तस्तपस्त्यक्त्वा मुनीश्वरः ॥ 48 ॥
4.24.m:
The union of the clever woman with the clever man was equal;
abandoning austerity, the lord of sages became attached to domestic life. // 48

4.24.s:
karoti kalahe nityaṃ kandalī svāminā saha ..
munīndro bodhayāmāsa nītivākyena kāminīm ..
sā tanna bubudhe kiṃcitkaroti kalahe spṛhām .. 49 ..
4.24.d:
करोति कलहे नित्यं कन्दली स्वामिना सह ॥
मुनीन्द्रो बोधयामास नीतिवाक्येन कामिनीम् ॥
सा तन्न बुबुधे किंचित्करोति कलहे स्पृहाम् ॥ 49 ॥

4.24.s:
tātapradattajñānena sā na śāntā babhūva ha ..
na hīyate prabodhena svabhāvo duratikramaḥ ..4.24.50..
4.24.d:
तातप्रदत्तज्ञानेन सा न शान्ता बभूव ह ॥
न हीयते प्रबोधेन स्वभावो दुरतिक्रमः ॥4.24.50॥
4.24.m:
She did not become calmed by the wisdom imparted by her father;
one's inborn nature, being hard to overcome, is not eliminated by admonition.

4.24.s:
nityaṃ kaṭūktiṃ kāntaṃ sā karoti hetunā vinā ..
jagatprakampitaṃ yena tayā kopātsa kampitaḥ..51..
4.24.d:
नित्यं कटूक्तिं कान्तं सा करोति हेतुना विना ॥
जगत्प्रकम्पितं येन तया कोपात्स कम्पितः॥51॥
4.24.m:
Constantly she spoke harsh words to her beloved without any cause;
he by whom the world was made to tremble was himself made to tremble by her in anger.

4.24.s:
tayā kṛtāṃ kaṭūktiṃ ca kṣamāsaṃsthāṃ cakāra ha ..
bodhayāmāsa tāṃ nityaṃ sadyo mohāddayānidhiḥ .. 52 ..
4.24.d:
तया कृतां कटूक्तिं च क्षमासंस्थां चकार ह ॥
बोधयामास तां नित्यं सद्यो मोहाद्दयानिधिः ॥ 52 ॥
4.24.m:
Yet the harsh words spoken by her he consistently endured with forgiveness;
out of compassion, that ocean of mercy constantly admonished her at once from her delusion.

4.24.s:
kaṭūktiśatakaṃ pūrṇaṃ tatkālena babhūva ha ..
kṣamāṃ cakāra kṛpayā kaṭūktiṃ ca śatādhikām .. 53 ..
4.24.d:
कटूक्तिशतकं पूर्णं तत्कालेन बभूव ह ॥
क्षमां चकार कृपया कटूक्तिं च शताधिकाम् ॥ 53 ॥
4.24.m:
In time, a full hundred of her harsh words came to pass;
mercifully, he forgave even more than a hundred harsh words.

4.24.s:
patnīkaṭūktyā niyataṃ pradagdhaṃ mānasaṃ muneḥ ..
tasyāḥ kaṭūktikāriṇyāḥ karma pūrṇaṃ babhūva ha .. 54 ..
4.24.d:
पत्नीकटूक्त्या नियतं प्रदग्धं मानसं मुनेः ॥
तस्याः कटूक्तिकारिण्याः कर्म पूर्णं बभूव ह ॥ 54 ॥
4.24.m:
The sage's mind was continually scorched by the harsh words of his wife;
the karma of that woman who uttered harsh words was now fulfilled.

4.24.s:
svātmārāmo dayāluśca kopaṃ tyaktuṃ na sa kṣamaḥ ..
śaśāpa kāminīṃ mohādbhasmarāśirbhaveti ca .. 55 ..
4.24.d:
स्वात्मारामो दयालुश्च कोपं त्यक्तुं न स क्षमः ॥
शशाप कामिनीं मोहाद्भस्मराशिर्भवेति च ॥ 55 ॥
4.24.m:
Though rejoicing in his own Self and compassionate, he could not let go of his anger;
out of delusion he cursed his beloved, saying: “Become a heap of ashes!”

4.24.s:
muneriṅgitamātreṇa bhasmasātsā babhūva ha ..
evamatyucchritānāṃ ca na kalyāṇaṃ jagattraye .. 56..
4.24.d:
मुनेरिङ्गितमात्रेण भस्मसात्सा बभूव ह ॥
एवमत्युच्छ्रितानां च न कल्याणं जगत्त्रये ॥ 56॥
4.24.m:
At a mere gesture from the sage, she was reduced to ashes.
Thus for those who are excessively arrogant, there is no welfare in the three worlds.

4.24.s:
śarīre bhasmasādbhūte pratibiṃbaḥ sa cātmanaḥ ..
jīvastatrāntarikṣastho hyuvāca vinayātprabhum .. 57 ..
4.24.d:
शरीरे भस्मसाद्भूते प्रतिबिंबः स चात्मनः ॥
जीवस्तत्रान्तरिक्षस्थो ह्युवाच विनयात्प्रभुम् ॥ 57 ॥
4.24.m:
When her body was reduced to ashes, that reflection of the Self,
the individual soul standing in mid-air, humbly said to the master:

4.24.s:
jīva uvāca ..
he nātha sarvadarśī tvaṃ satataṃ jñānacakṣuṣā ..
sarvaṃ jānāsi sarvajñaḥ kimahaṃ bodhayāmi te.. 58 ..
4.24.d:
जीव उवाच ॥
हे नाथ सर्वदर्शी त्वं सततं ज्ञानचक्षुषा ॥
सर्वं जानासि सर्वज्ञः किमहं बोधयामि ते॥ 58 ॥
4.24.m:
“O master, you are all-seeing at all times through the eye of wisdom;
all-knowing, you know everything; what can I teach you?

4.24.s:
saduktirvā kaṭūktirvā kopaḥ saṃtāpa eva ca..
lobho mohaśca kāmaśca kṣutpipāsādikaṃ ca yat ..59..
4.24.d:
सदुक्तिर्वा कटूक्तिर्वा कोपः संताप एव च॥
लोभो मोहश्च कामश्च क्षुत्पिपासादिकं च यत् ॥59॥
4.24.m:
Good speech or harsh speech, anger and torment,
greed, delusion, lust, and whatever hunger and thirst there be;

4.24.s:
sthaulyaṃ kārśyaṃ ca nāśaśca dṛśyādṛśyaṃ samudbhavam ..
sarvaṃ śarīradharmaṃ ca na jīvasya na cātmanaḥ ..4.24.60..
4.24.d:
स्थौल्यं कार्श्यं च नाशश्च दृश्यादृश्यं समुद्भवम् ॥
सर्वं शरीरधर्मं च न जीवस्य न चात्मनः ॥4.24.60॥
4.24.m:
stoutness, emaciation, destruction, and birth both visible and invisible —
all these are properties of the body, neither of the soul nor of the Self.

4.24.s:
sattvaṃ rajastama iti śarīraṃ triguṇātmakam ..
tacca nānāprakāraṃ ca nibodha kathayāmi te ..61..
4.24.d:
सत्त्वं रजस्तम इति शरीरं त्रिगुणात्मकम् ॥
तच्च नानाप्रकारं च निबोध कथयामि ते ॥61॥
4.24.m:
The body is composed of the three gunas: sattva, rajas, and tamas;
and it has many forms; listen, I shall explain it to you.

4.24.s:
kiñcitsattvātiriktaṃ ca kiñcideva rajodhikam ..
tamotiriktaṃ kiñcicca na samaṃ kutracinmune ..62..
4.24.d:
किञ्चित्सत्त्वातिरिक्तं च किञ्चिदेव रजोधिकम् ॥
तमोतिरिक्तं किञ्चिच्च न समं कुत्रचिन्मुने ॥62॥
4.24.m:
One [body] has an excess of sattva, another has an excess of rajas,
and one has an excess of tamas; it is never equal anywhere, O sage.

4.24.s:
sattvodayācca muktīcchā karmecchā ca rajoguṇāt..
tamoguṇājjīvahiṃsā kopo'haṃkāra eva ca .. 63 ..
4.24.d:
सत्त्वोदयाच्च मुक्तीच्छा कर्मेच्छा च रजोगुणात्॥
तमोगुणाज्जीवहिंसा कोपोऽहंकार एव च ॥ 63 ॥
4.24.m:
From the rise of sattva comes the desire for liberation, and from the quality of rajas the desire for action;
from the quality of tamas comes injury to living beings, anger, and egoism.

4.24.s:
kopātkaṭūktirniyataṃ kaṭūktyā śatrutā bhavet ..
tayā cāpriyatā sadyaḥ śatruḥ kaḥ kasya bhūtale .. 64 ..
4.24.d:
कोपात्कटूक्तिर्नियतं कटूक्त्या शत्रुता भवेत् ॥
तया चाप्रियता सद्यः शत्रुः कः कस्य भूतले ॥ 64 ॥
4.24.m:
From anger comes harsh speech without fail; through harsh speech enmity arises;
and through that comes sudden antipathy. On the face of the earth, who is an enemy to whom?

4.24.s:
ko vā priyo'priyaḥ kaḥ kiṃ kiṃ mitraṃ ko ripurbhavet ..
iṃdriyāṇi ca bījāni sarvatra śatrumitrayoḥ ..65..
4.24.d:
को वा प्रियोऽप्रियः कः किं किं मित्रं को रिपुर्भवेत् ॥
इंद्रियाणि च बीजानि सर्वत्र शत्रुमित्रयोः ॥65॥
4.24.m:
Or who is dear, who is disliked, who is what? Who can be a friend, who an enemy?
Everywhere the senses alone are the causes of enemies and friends.

4.24.s:
prāṇādhikaḥ priyaḥ strīṇāṃ bhartuḥ prāṇādhikā priyā ..
babhūva śatrutā sadyo duruktyā ca kṣaṇāddvayoḥ .. 66 ..
4.24.d:
प्राणाधिकः प्रियः स्त्रीणां भर्तुः प्राणाधिका प्रिया ॥
बभूव शत्रुता सद्यो दुरुक्त्या च क्षणाद्द्वयोः ॥ 66 ॥
4.24.m:
The husband is dearer than life to wives; the wife is dearer than life to the husband;
yet in an instant, through ill speech, enmity immediately arose between the two.

4.24.s:
yadgataṃ tadgataṃ sarvaṃ kāmadoṣeṇa vai prabho ..
kṣamāparādhaṃ nikhilaṃ kiṃ kartavyaṃ vadādhunā .. 67 ..
4.24.d:
यद्गतं तद्गतं सर्वं कामदोषेण वै प्रभो ॥
क्षमापराधं निखिलं किं कर्तव्यं वदाधुना ॥ 67 ॥
4.24.m:
What is gone is completely gone, O master, indeed through the fault of desire;
forgive all offenses! Tell me now what should be done.

4.24.s:
kiṃ karomi kva yāmīti bhavitā kutra janma me ..
tava nānyasya jāyā'haṃ bhaviṣyāmi jagattraye .. 68 ..
4.24.d:
किं करोमि क्व यामीति भविता कुत्र जन्म मे ॥
तव नान्यस्य जायाऽहं भविष्यामि जगत्त्रये ॥ 68 ॥
4.24.m:
What shall I do? Where shall I go? Where will my birth take place?
In the three worlds I shall be your wife, and no one else’s!”

4.24.s:
ityevamuktvā jīvaśca maunībhūto babhūva ha ..
mūrcchāmavāpa sa muniḥ śokena hṛtacetanaḥ .. 69 ..
4.24.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा जीवश्च मौनीभूतो बभूव ह ॥
मूर्च्छामवाप स मुनिः शोकेन हृतचेतनः ॥ 69 ॥
4.24.m:
Having spoken thus, the soul fell silent;
the sage fainted, his consciousness robbed by grief.

4.24.s:
svātmārāmo mahājñānī jahāra cetanāmaho ..
strīvicchedo vidagdhānāṃ sarvaśokātparātparaḥ .. 4.24.70 ..
4.24.d:
स्वात्मारामो महाज्ञानी जहार चेतनामहो ॥
स्त्रीविच्छेदो विदग्धानां सर्वशोकात्परात्परः ॥ 4.24.70 ॥
4.24.m:
Rejoicing in his own Self, a possessor of great wisdom — ah, he lost consciousness!
For the wise, separation from a wife is higher than any other grief.

4.24.s:
kṣaṇena cetanāṃ prāpya prāṇāṃstyaktuṃ samudyataḥ ..
tatra yogāsanaṃ kṛtvā cakāra vāyudhāraṇam ..71..
4.24.d:
क्षणेन चेतनां प्राप्य प्राणांस्त्यक्तुं समुद्यतः ॥
तत्र योगासनं कृत्वा चकार वायुधारणम् ॥71॥
4.24.m:
Regaining consciousness after a moment, he prepared to abandon his life breaths;
assuming a yoga posture there, he practiced breath retention.

4.24.s:
etasminnantare tatra jagāma brāhmaṇo'rbhakaḥ..
daṇḍī chatrī raktavāsā bibhratti lakamuttmam .. 72 ..
4.24.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र जगाम ब्राह्मणोऽर्भकः॥
दण्डी छत्री रक्तवासा बिभ्रत्ति लकमुत्त्मम् ॥ 72 ॥
4.24.m:
In the meantime, a young Brahmin boy arrived there,
holding a staff and an umbrella, wearing red garments, and bearing an excellent tilaka,

4.24.s:
sasmitaḥ śyāmavarṇaśca prajvalanbrahmatejasā ..
vayasā'tiśiśuḥ śānto jñānī vedavidāṃ varaḥ .. 73 ..
4.24.d:
सस्मितः श्यामवर्णश्च प्रज्वलन्ब्रह्मतेजसा ॥
वयसाऽतिशिशुः शान्तो ज्ञानी वेदविदां वरः ॥ 73 ॥
4.24.m:
smiling, dark-complexioned, blazing with the splendour of Brahman,
very young in age, tranquil, wise, the foremost of the knowers of the Vedas.

4.24.s:
dṛṣṭvā taṃ saṃbhrameṇaiva durvāsāḥ praṇanāma ha ..
vāsayāmāsa tatraiva pūjayāmāsa bhaktitaḥ .. 74 ..
4.24.d:
दृष्ट्वा तं संभ्रमेणैव दुर्वासाः प्रणनाम ह ॥
वासयामास तत्रैव पूजयामास भक्तितः ॥ 74 ॥
4.24.m:
Seeing him, Durvāsas bowed down in reverence;
he seated him right there and worshipped him with devotion.

4.24.s:
uvāca brāhmaṇavaṭurdattvā tasmai sadāśiṣam ..
taddarśanādāśiṣā ca sarvaṃ duḥkhaṃ gataṃ muneḥ .. 75 ..
4.24.d:
उवाच ब्राह्मणवटुर्दत्त्वा तस्मै सदाशिषम् ॥
तद्दर्शनादाशिषा च सर्वं दुःखं गतं मुनेः ॥ 75 ॥
4.24.m:
The young Brahmin celibate, having given him an auspicious blessing, spoke;
by seeing him and receiving his blessing, all the sorrow of the sage vanished.

4.24.s:
śiśurūpaṃ kṣaṇaṃ sthitvā tamuvāca vicakṣaṇaḥ ..
pīyūṣatulyaṃ nītyoghaṃ nītiśāstraṃ viśāradaḥ .. 76 ..
4.24.d:
शिशुरूपं क्षणं स्थित्वा तमुवाच विचक्षणः ॥
पीयूषतुल्यं नीत्योघं नीतिशास्त्रं विशारदः ॥ 76 ॥
4.24.m:
Having remained a moment in the form of a child, that wise one spoke to him;
expert in the treatises of statecraft, he uttered an outpouring of conduct resembling nectar.

4.24.s:
śiśuruvāca ..
sarvaṃ jānāsi sarvajña gurormantraprasādataḥ ..
kiṃ tattvaṃ tvāmahaṃ vipra pṛcchāmi śokakātaram .. 77 ..
4.24.d:
शिशुरुवाच ॥
सर्वं जानासि सर्वज्ञ गुरोर्मन्त्रप्रसादतः ॥
किं तत्त्वं त्वामहं विप्र पृच्छामि शोककातरम् ॥ 77 ॥
4.24.m:
“All-knowing one, you know everything by the grace of your guru’s mantra;
O Brahmin, what truth can I ask of you, agitated as you are by grief?

4.24.s:
brāhmaṇānāṃ tapo dharmastapaḥsādhyaṃ jagattrayam ..
svadharmaṃ vai parityajya kimidānīṃ karoṣi bhoḥ .. 78 ..
4.24.d:
ब्राह्मणानां तपो धर्मस्तपःसाध्यं जगत्त्रयम् ॥
स्वधर्मं वै परित्यज्य किमिदानीं करोषि भोः ॥ 78 ॥
4.24.m:
For Brahmins, asceticism is the sacred duty; the three worlds are mastered by asceticism.
having abandoned your own duty, what are you doing now, sir?

4.24.s:
kā kasya patnī kaḥ kāntaḥ kasyā vā bhuvanatraye ..
mūrkhāṇāṃ vañcanāṃ kartuṃ karoti māyayā hariḥ .. 79 ..
4.24.d:
का कस्य पत्नी कः कान्तः कस्या वा भुवनत्रये ॥
मूर्खाणां वञ्चनां कर्तुं करोति मायया हरिः ॥ 79 ॥
4.24.m:
Who is whose wife, or who is whose husband in the three worlds?
In order to delude fools, Hari creates [this] by his māyā.

4.24.s:
mithyā patnī taveyaṃ ca kṣaṇāttena gatādhunā ..
na hi satyamadṛśyaṃ ca mithyā yatrācirasthitiḥ .. 4.24.80 ..
4.24.d:
मिथ्या पत्नी तवेयं च क्षणात्तेन गताधुना ॥
न हि सत्यमदृश्यं च मिथ्या यत्राचिरस्थितिः ॥ 4.24.80 ॥
4.24.m:
This wife of yours was unreal; therefore she is gone in an instant now.
For what is invisible is not real, and that which is of fleeting duration is false.

4.24.s:
ekānaṃśā ca bhaginī vasudevasutā hareḥ..
pārvatyaṃśasamudbhūtā suśīlā cirajīvinī ..81 ..
4.24.d:
एकानंशा च भगिनी वसुदेवसुता हरेः॥
पार्वत्यंशसमुद्भूता सुशीला चिरजीविनी ॥81 ॥
4.24.m:
Hari's sister, Ekānaṃśā, the daughter of Vasudeva,
born from a portion of Pārvatī, of good character and long-lived,

4.24.s:
kalpe kalpe sundarī sā tava patnī bhaviṣyati ..
mano dehi tapasyāyāṃ mudā katipayaṃ dinam..82..
4.24.d:
कल्पे कल्पे सुन्दरी सा तव पत्नी भविष्यति ॥
मनो देहि तपस्यायां मुदा कतिपयं दिनम्॥82॥
4.24.m:
that fair lady will become your wife aeon after aeon.
Direct your mind to austerities with joy for a few days.

4.24.s:
kandalī kadalījātirbhaviṣyati mahītale ..
śubhadā phaladā kāntā sakṛtsūtā sudurlabhā .. 83 ..
4.24.d:
कन्दली कदलीजातिर्भविष्यति महीतले ॥
शुभदा फलदा कान्ता सकृत्सूता सुदुर्लभा ॥ 83 ॥
4.24.m:
Kandalī will become the plantain species on the face of the earth,
bringing auspiciousness, bearing fruit, lovely, bearing offspring only once, and very rare.

4.24.s:
kalpāntare śāntarūpā tava patnī bhaviṣya ti..
atyucchrisya damanamucitaṃ ca śrutau śrutam.. 84..
4.24.d:
कल्पान्तरे शान्तरूपा तव पत्नी भविष्य ति॥
अत्युच्छ्रिस्य दमनमुचितं च श्रुतौ श्रुतम्॥ 84॥
4.24.m:
In another aeon, tranquil in form, she will become your wife.
The subduing of the excessively haughty is proper and heard in the Veda.”

4.24.s:
ityevamuktvā śīghraṃ ca viprarūpī janārdanaḥ ..
dattvā jñānaṃ ca viprāya so'ntardhānaṃ cakāra ha .. 85 ..
4.24.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा शीघ्रं च विप्ररूपी जनार्दनः ॥
दत्त्वा ज्ञानं च विप्राय सोऽन्तर्धानं चकार ह ॥ 85 ॥
4.24.m:
Having spoken thus, Janārdana, in the form of a brāhmaṇa, quickly
imparted knowledge to the brāhmaṇa and vanished.

4.24.s:
muniḥ sarvabhramaṃ tyaktvā tapasyāyāṃ mano dadhe ..
kandalī kadalījātirbabhūva dharaṇītale .. 86 ..
4.24.d:
मुनिः सर्वभ्रमं त्यक्त्वा तपस्यायां मनो दधे ॥
कन्दली कदलीजातिर्बभूव धरणीतले ॥ 86 ॥
4.24.m:
The sage, casting off all delusion, set his mind on austerities.
Kandalī became the plantain species on the surface of the earth.

4.24.s:
daityastālavanaṃ gatvā babhūva gardabhākṛtiḥ ..
tilottamā bāṇaputrī babhūva samaye mune .. 87..
4.24.d:
दैत्यस्तालवनं गत्वा बभूव गर्दभाकृतिः ॥
तिलोत्तमा बाणपुत्री बभूव समये मुने ॥ 87॥
4.24.m:
The Daitya went to the palm forest and assumed the form of an ass;
Tilottamā became the daughter of Bāṇa in due course, O sage.

4.24.s:
daityendro viṣṇucakreṇa prāṇāṃstyaktvā suvāñchitam ..
saṃprāpya caraṇāmbhojaṃ munerapi sudurlabham .. 88 ..
4.24.d:
दैत्येन्द्रो विष्णुचक्रेण प्राणांस्त्यक्त्वा सुवाञ्छितम् ॥
संप्राप्य चरणाम्भोजं मुनेरपि सुदुर्लभम् ॥ 88 ॥
4.24.m:
The lord of the Daityas, relinquishing his life-breaths by Viṣṇu's discus, attained the longed-for
lotus feet, which are very difficult even for sages to attain.

4.24.s:
kāle tilottamā bhūtvā jagāma svālayaṃ punaḥ ..
kṛṣṇapautrāliṃganena paripūrṇamanorathā .. 89 ..
4.24.d:
काले तिलोत्तमा भूत्वा जगाम स्वालयं पुनः ॥
कृष्णपौत्रालिंगनेन परिपूर्णमनोरथा ॥ 89 ॥
4.24.m:
Tilottamā, having attained [that form] in time, returned to her own abode again,
her desire fully fulfilled by the embrace of Kṛṣṇa's grandson.

4.24.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ śrutvā śrīkṛṣṇākhyānamuttamam ..
padepade sundaraṃ ca kiṃ bhūyaḥ śrotumicchasi .. 4.24.90 ..
4.24.d:
इत्येवं कथितं श्रुत्वा श्रीकृष्णाख्यानमुत्तमम् ॥
पदेपदे सुन्दरं च किं भूयः श्रोतुमिच्छसि ॥ 4.24.90 ॥
4.24.m:
Having heard this excellent narrative of Śrī Kṛṣṇa told in this manner,
which is beautiful at every step, what do you wish to hear further?

4.25.s:
.. nārada uvāca .. ..
śrutaṃ kimadbhutaṃ brahman hareścaritamaṅgalam ..
viśeṣatastava mukhe hyatīva sumanoharam .. 1 ..
4.25.d:
॥ नारद उवाच ॥ ॥
श्रुतं किमद्भुतं ब्रह्मन् हरेश्चरितमङ्गलम् ॥
विशेषतस्तव मुखे ह्यतीव सुमनोहरम् ॥ 1 ॥

4.25.s:
mṛtāyāṃ munikanyāyāṃ śāpāddurvāsaso muneḥ ..
kiṃ cakāra samāgatya tanme brūhi tapodhana .. 2 ..
4.25.d:
मृतायां मुनिकन्यायां शापाद्दुर्वाससो मुनेः ॥
किं चकार समागत्य तन्मे ब्रूहि तपोधन ॥ 2 ॥

4.25.s:
.. śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca .. ..
sarasvatīnadītīre tapasyāṃ kurvato muneḥ ..
papāta dhautamūrdhvācca dhāryamāṇaṃ ca vāyunā .. 3 ..
4.25.d:
॥ श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥ ॥
सरस्वतीनदीतीरे तपस्यां कुर्वतो मुनेः ॥
पपात धौतमूर्ध्वाच्च धार्यमाणं च वायुना ॥ 3 ॥

4.25.s:
pṛthivyāṃ patite vastre tapastyaktvā munīśvaraḥ ..
dhyānena bubudhe sarvaṃ kanyāsaṃbandhi saṃkaṭam..4..
4.25.d:
पृथिव्यां पतिते वस्त्रे तपस्त्यक्त्वा मुनीश्वरः ॥
ध्यानेन बुबुधे सर्वं कन्यासंबन्धि संकटम्॥4॥

4.25.s:
jagāma śokāviṣṭo'pi tūrṇaṃ jāmāturāśramam..
siṣeca pṛthivīreṇūcchaśvannayanabindunā ..5..
4.25.d:
जगाम शोकाविष्टोऽपि तूर्णं जामातुराश्रमम्॥
सिषेच पृथिवीरेणूच्छश्वन्नयनबिन्दुना ॥5॥

4.25.s:
gatvā''layasamīpaṃ ca vipraḥ kātaramānasaḥ ..
he vatse kandalītyevamuvāca ca punaḥpunaḥ.. .. 6 ..
4.25.d:
गत्वा'ऽलयसमीपं च विप्रः कातरमानसः ॥
हे वत्से कन्दलीत्येवमुवाच च पुनःपुनः॥ ॥ 6 ॥

4.25.s:
śvaśarasya svaraṃ jñātvā durvāsā bhayavihvalaḥ ..
bahirbabhūva śīghraṃ ca papāta caraṇāmbuje .. 7 ..
4.25.d:
श्वशरस्य स्वरं ज्ञात्वा दुर्वासा भयविह्वलः ॥
बहिर्बभूव शीघ्रं च पपात चरणाम्बुजे ॥ 7 ॥

4.25.s:
praṇamya śvaśuraṃ śokādvilalāpa bhṛśaṃ punaḥ ..
pravṛttiṃ kathayāmāsa mūlato munisattamam .. 8 ..
4.25.d:
प्रणम्य श्वशुरं शोकाद्विललाप भृशं पुनः ॥
प्रवृत्तिं कथयामास मूलतो मुनिसत्तमम् ॥ 8 ॥

4.25.s:
śrutvā vārtāṃ śucā''viṣṭaḥ papāta dharaṇītale ..
mūrcchāmāpa mahājñānī niśceṣṭo hi yathā mṛtaḥ .. 9 ..
4.25.d:
श्रुत्वा वार्तां शुचा'ऽविष्टः पपात धरणीतले ॥
मूर्च्छामाप महाज्ञानी निश्चेष्टो हि यथा मृतः ॥ 9 ॥

4.25.s:
mṛtaṃ dṛṣṭvā sa durvāsā mune manasi saṃkaṭam ..
cetanāṃ kārayāmāsa prayatnena mahāmuneḥ .. 4.25.10 ..
4.25.d:
मृतं दृष्ट्वा स दुर्वासा मुने मनसि संकटम् ॥
चेतनां कारयामास प्रयत्नेन महामुनेः ॥ 4.25.10 ॥

4.25.s:
saṃprāpya cetanāṃ śīghramuvāca taṃ puraḥ sthitam ..
jāmātaraṃ śokayutaṃ bhītaṃ praṇatakandharam .. 11 ..
4.25.d:
संप्राप्य चेतनां शीघ्रमुवाच तं पुरः स्थितम् ॥
जामातरं शोकयुतं भीतं प्रणतकन्धरम् ॥ 11 ॥

4.25.s:
mahāśokādaśrupūrṇaṃ raktapaṅkajalocanam ..
kopātkampitavāñchaśvatsaṃtrastaḥ sphuritādharaḥ .. 12 ..
4.25.d:
महाशोकादश्रुपूर्णं रक्तपङ्कजलोचनम् ॥
कोपात्कम्पितवाञ्छश्वत्संत्रस्तः स्फुरिताधरः ॥ 12 ॥

4.25.s:
aurva uvāca ..
aye brahmannatrivaṃśa pautrastvaṃ jagatīpateḥ ..
svalpadoṣe bahutaraḥ kṛto daṇḍastvayā katham ..13..
4.25.d:
और्व उवाच ॥
अये ब्रह्मन्नत्रिवंश पौत्रस्त्वं जगतीपतेः ॥
स्वल्पदोषे बहुतरः कृतो दण्डस्त्वया कथम् ॥13॥

4.25.s:
tvajjanma śaṃkarāṃśena śiṣyastasya jagadguroḥ ..
vedavedāṅgavijñaśca sarvajño guṇavānsvayam .. 14 ..
4.25.d:
त्वज्जन्म शंकरांशेन शिष्यस्तस्य जगद्गुरोः ॥
वेदवेदाङ्गविज्ञश्च सर्वज्ञो गुणवान्स्वयम् ॥ 14 ॥

4.25.s:
anasūyā mahāsādhvī kamalāṃśā tava prasūḥ ..
na jāne kena doṣeṇa tava caitādṛśī matiḥ .. 15 ..
4.25.d:
अनसूया महासाध्वी कमलांशा तव प्रसूः ॥
न जाने केन दोषेण तव चैतादृशी मतिः ॥ 15 ॥

4.25.s:
guṇavāñjanako yasya mātā guṇavatī satī ..
tayoḥ putro dayāhīno gatiḥ sūkṣmā śruteraho .. 16 ..
4.25.d:
गुणवाञ्जनको यस्य माता गुणवती सती ॥
तयोः पुत्रो दयाहीनो गतिः सूक्ष्मा श्रुतेरहो ॥ 16 ॥

4.25.s:
mama prāṇādhikā kanyā mudā tvayi samarpitā..
mahāguṇānvitā svalpadoṣeṇa parimiśritā .. 17 ..
4.25.d:
मम प्राणाधिका कन्या मुदा त्वयि समर्पिता॥
महागुणान्विता स्वल्पदोषेण परिमिश्रिता ॥ 17 ॥

4.25.s:
vāgduṣṭāyāśca daṇḍo hi parityāgaḥ śrutau śrutaḥ ..
tvayā krodhādyadi tyaktā pitrā yatnena pālitā ..18..
4.25.d:
वाग्दुष्टायाश्च दण्डो हि परित्यागः श्रुतौ श्रुतः ॥
त्वया क्रोधाद्यदि त्यक्ता पित्रा यत्नेन पालिता ॥18॥

4.25.s:
madapatyaṃ svalpadoṣe yato bhasmīkṛtaṃ tvayā ..
parābhavastava mahānbhaviṣyati na saṃśayaḥ .. 19 ..
4.25.d:
मदपत्यं स्वल्पदोषे यतो भस्मीकृतं त्वया ॥
पराभवस्तव महान्भविष्यति न संशयः ॥ 19 ॥

4.25.s:
mahatāṃ kṣudrajantūnāṃ sarveṣāṃ jīvināṃ sadā ..
sraṣṭā pātā ca śāstā ca bhagavānkaruṇānidhiḥ .. 4.25.20 ..
4.25.d:
महतां क्षुद्रजन्तूनां सर्वेषां जीविनां सदा ॥
स्रष्टा पाता च शास्ता च भगवान्करुणानिधिः ॥ 4.25.20 ॥

4.25.s:
ityuktvā ca muniśreṣṭho vilapya ca punaḥ punaḥ ..
he'mba vatse hyayītyuktvā jagāma svālayaṃ ruṣā ..21..
4.25.d:
इत्युक्त्वा च मुनिश्रेष्ठो विलप्य च पुनः पुनः ॥
हेऽम्ब वत्से ह्ययीत्युक्त्वा जगाम स्वालयं रुषा ॥21॥
4.25.m:
Having spoken thus, the best of sages, lamenting again and again,
saying, 'Ah, mother! Child! Alas!', departed to his own abode in anger.

4.25.s:
gate munīndre durvāsā vilalāpa bhṛśaṃ punaḥ ..
jñānena vismṛtaḥ śoko babhūva dviguṇaḥ punaḥ .. 22 ..
4.25.d:
गते मुनीन्द्रे दुर्वासा विललाप भृशं पुनः ॥
ज्ञानेन विस्मृतः शोको बभूव द्विगुणः पुनः ॥ 22 ॥
4.25.m:
When the great sage had gone, Durvāsas lamented bitterly again;
the grief that had been forgotten through knowledge doubled once more.

4.25.s:
śokānalo hi kālena vicchinno jñānabhasmanā ..
bandhudarśanaśuṣkendhadānena vardhate punaḥ .. .. 23 ..
4.25.d:
शोकानलो हि कालेन विच्छिन्नो ज्ञानभस्मना ॥
बन्धुदर्शनशुष्केन्धदानेन वर्धते पुनः ॥ ॥ 23 ॥
4.25.m:
For the fire of grief, interrupted in time by the ash of knowledge,
grows again through the offering of the dry fuel that is the sight of a relative.

4.25.s:
smāraṃsmāraṃ priyāṃ tatra vilapya ca punaḥpunaḥ ..
bodhayitvā svamātmānaṃ tapasyāyāṃ mano dadhau .. 24 ..
4.25.d:
स्मारंस्मारं प्रियां तत्र विलप्य च पुनःपुनः ॥
बोधयित्वा स्वमात्मानं तपस्यायां मनो दधौ ॥ 24 ॥
4.25.m:
Remembering and remembering his beloved there, and lamenting again and again,
he enlightened himself and set his mind on asceticism.

4.25.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ muneḥ śāpasya kāraṇam ..
babhūva tasya kālena duḥsahaśca parābhavaḥ .. 25 ..
4.25.d:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं मुनेः शापस्य कारणम् ॥
बभूव तस्य कालेन दुःसहश्च पराभवः ॥ 25 ॥
4.25.m:
Thus the whole cause of the sage's curse has been told.
In the course of time, his downfall became unbearable.

4.25.s:
nārada uvāca ..
durvāsāḥ śaṃkarasyāṃśaḥ śivatulyaśca tejasā ..
tejasvī ko mahāneva cakāra tatparābhavam .. 26 ..
4.25.d:
नारद उवाच ॥
दुर्वासाः शंकरस्यांशः शिवतुल्यश्च तेजसा ॥
तेजस्वी को महानेव चकार तत्पराभवम् ॥ 26 ॥
4.25.m:
Durvāsas is a portion of Śaṅkara and equal to Śiva in brilliance;
what great radiant one brought about his downfall?

4.25.s:
śrīnārāyaṇa uvāca ..
ambarīṣo hi rājendraḥ sūryavaṃśasamudbhavaḥ ..
śrīkṛṣṇacaraṇāmbhoje tanmanāḥ saṃtataṃ mune .. 27 ..*
4.25.d:
श्रीनारायण उवाच ॥
अम्बरीषो हि राजेन्द्रः सूर्यवंशसमुद्भवः ॥
श्रीकृष्णचरणाम्भोजे तन्मनाः संततं मुने ॥ 27 ॥*
4.25.m:
There was a king of kings named Ambarīṣa, born in the solar dynasty,
his mind always fixed upon the lotus feet of Śrī Kṛṣṇa, O sage. / Not on kingdoms, nor on wives, nor on sons, nor on subjects,

4.25.s:
na rājyeṣu na bhāryāsu na putreṣu prajāsu ca ..
na saṃpatsu kṣaṇaṃ cittaṃ puṇyakarmārjiṃtāsu ca .. 28 ..
4.25.d:
न राज्येषु न भार्यासु न पुत्रेषु प्रजासु च ॥
न संपत्सु क्षणं चित्तं पुण्यकर्मार्जिंतासु च ॥ 28 ॥
4.25.m: nor on riches acquired through meritorious deeds was his mind set, even for a moment.

4.25.s:
dhyāyate'harniśaṃ dharmī svante jñāne hariṃ mudā ..
mahājitendriyaḥ śānto viṣṇuvrataparāyaṇaḥ .. 29 ..
4.25.d:
ध्यायतेऽहर्निशं धर्मी स्वन्ते ज्ञाने हरिं मुदा ॥
महाजितेन्द्रियः शान्तो विष्णुव्रतपरायणः ॥ 29 ॥
4.25.m:
Righteous, he joyfully meditated on Hari day and night in his inner consciousness;
he had utterly conquered his senses, was tranquil, and was devoted to the observances of Viṣṇu,

4.25.s:
ekādaśī vratarataḥ kṛṣṇapūjāsu tatparaḥ ..
sarvakarmasvaliptaśca kartā kṛṣṇārpiteṣu ca ..4.25.30..
4.25.d:
एकादशी व्रतरतः कृष्णपूजासु तत्परः ॥
सर्वकर्मस्वलिप्तश्च कर्ता कृष्णार्पितेषु च ॥4.25.30॥
4.25.m:
devoted to the Ekādaśī observance, intent upon the worship of Kṛṣṇa,
unstained by all actions, and an agent in things offered to Kṛṣṇa.

4.25.s:
sutīkṣṇaṃ ṣoḍaśāraṃ ca hareścakraṃ sudarśanam ..
tejasā haritulyaṃ ca sūryakoṭisamaprabham .. 31 ..
4.25.d:
सुतीक्ष्णं षोडशारं च हरेश्चक्रं सुदर्शनम् ॥
तेजसा हरितुल्यं च सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम् ॥ 31 ॥
4.25.m:
Hari's very sharp Sudarśana discus of sixteen spokes,
equal to Hari in splendor, radiant as ten million suns,

4.25.s:
brahmādibhiḥ stūyamānaṃ pūjitaṃ ca surāsuraiḥ ..
prabhuṇā rakṣitaṃ śaśvadrakṣāyai nṛpasannidhau .. .. 32 ..
4.25.d:
ब्रह्मादिभिः स्तूयमानं पूजितं च सुरासुरैः ॥
प्रभुणा रक्षितं शश्वद्रक्षायै नृपसन्निधौ ॥ ॥ 32 ॥
4.25.m:
praised by Brahmā and the others, and worshipped by gods and asuras,
was stationed by the Lord constantly beside the king for his protection.

4.25.s:
ekādaśīvrataṃ kṛtvā dvādaśīdivase sati ..
snātvā vidhāya pūjāṃ ca kālena vidhipūrvakam ..33..
4.25.d:
एकादशीव्रतं कृत्वा द्वादशीदिवसे सति ॥
स्नात्वा विधाय पूजां च कालेन विधिपूर्वकम् ॥33॥
4.25.m:
Having observed the Ekādaśī fast, when the Dvādaśī day arrived,
having bathed and performed worship in due time according to rule,

4.25.s:
dattvā dānaṃ brāhmaṇebhyaḥ suvarṇarajatādikam ..
brāhmaṇānbhojayitvā ca bhojanārthamuvāsa ha .. 34 ..
4.25.d:
दत्त्वा दानं ब्राह्मणेभ्यः सुवर्णरजतादिकम् ॥
ब्राह्मणान्भोजयित्वा च भोजनार्थमुवास ह ॥ 34 ॥
4.25.m:
having given gifts of gold, silver, and other things to brāhmaṇas,
and having fed the brāhmaṇas, he sat down to eat.

4.25.s:
etasminnantare viprastapasvī kṣudhito mune ..
daṇḍī chatrī śuklavāsā bibhrattilakamuttamam .. 35 ..
4.25.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे विप्रस्तपस्वी क्षुधितो मुने ॥
दण्डी छत्री शुक्लवासा बिभ्रत्तिलकमुत्तमम् ॥ 35 ॥
4.25.m:
At that moment, O sage, an ascetic brāhmaṇa, hungry,
holding a staff, an umbrella, wearing white garments, and bearing an excellent tilaka,

4.25.s:
jaṭilo'tikṛśastrastaḥ śuṣkakaṇṭhoṣṭhatālukaḥ ..
tatrājagāma bhagavāndurvāsā nṛpateḥ puraḥ .. 36 ..
4.25.d:
जटिलोऽतिकृशस्त्रस्तः शुष्ककण्ठोष्ठतालुकः ॥
तत्राजगाम भगवान्दुर्वासा नृपतेः पुरः ॥ 36 ॥
4.25.m:
matted-haired, very emaciated, distressed, with dried throat, lips, and palate—
the venerable Durvāsas arrived there before the king.

4.25.s:
sa ca dṛṣṭvā munīndraṃ tamutthāya ca praṇamya ca ..
dattvā pādyaṃ ca saṃprītyā svarṇasiṃhāsanaṃ dadau .. 37 ..
4.25.d:
स च दृष्ट्वा मुनीन्द्रं तमुत्थाय च प्रणम्य च ॥
दत्त्वा पाद्यं च संप्रीत्या स्वर्णसिंहासनं ददौ ॥ 37 ॥
4.25.m:
Seeing that prince of sages, [the king] stood up, bowed down,
offered water for the feet, and gladly presented a golden throne.

4.25.s:
tasmai dattvā ''śiṣaṃ vipraḥ samuvāsa sukhāsane ..
papraccha rājā taṃ prītaḥ kā''jñā te vada kāmitam .. 38 ..
4.25.d:
तस्मै दत्त्वा 'ऽशिषं विप्रः समुवास सुखासने ॥
पप्रच्छ राजा तं प्रीतः का'ऽज्ञा ते वद कामितम् ॥ 38 ॥
4.25.m:
Having given him a blessing, the brāhmaṇa sat upon the comfortable seat.
The delighted king asked him: 'What is your command? Speak your wish.'

4.25.s:
nṛpendravacanaṃ śrutvā tamuvāca mahāmuniḥ..
bubhukṣitasya me rājandehyannaṃ vidhipūrvakam..39..
4.25.d:
नृपेन्द्रवचनं श्रुत्वा तमुवाच महामुनिः॥
बुभुक्षितस्य मे राजन्देह्यन्नं विधिपूर्वकम्॥39॥
4.25.m:
Hearing the words of the king of kings, the great sage said to him:
'I am hungry, O king; give me food according to rule.

4.25.s:
kiṃtvaghamarṣaṇamantraṃ tu japtvā''yāmyacireṇa vai ..
kṣaṇaṃ pratīkṣatāṃ rājannityuktvā ca gato muniḥ .. 4.25.40 ..
4.25.d:
किंत्वघमर्षणमन्त्रं तु जप्त्वा'ऽयाम्यचिरेण वै ॥
क्षणं प्रतीक्षतां राजन्नित्युक्त्वा च गतो मुनिः ॥ 4.25.40 ॥
4.25.m:
However, having chanted the Aghamarṣaṇa mantra, I shall return without delay;
wait for a moment, O king.' Having spoken thus, the sage departed.

4.25.s:
gate vipre tu rājarṣiścintāṃ prāpa duratyayām ..
vilokya vigataprāyāṃ dvādaśīṃ bhayasaṃyutaḥ .. 41 ..
4.25.d:
गते विप्रे तु राजर्षिश्चिन्तां प्राप दुरत्ययाम् ॥
विलोक्य विगतप्रायां द्वादशीं भयसंयुतः ॥ 41 ॥
4.25.m:
When the brāhmaṇa had gone, the royal sage fell into insurmountable anxiety,
seeing that Dvādaśī was almost over, and became filled with fear.

4.25.s:
etasminnantare tatra samāyāntaṃ guruṃ mudā ..
natvā nivedya sarvaṃ tu nṛpatiḥ samuvāca ha .. 42 ..
4.25.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे तत्र समायान्तं गुरुं मुदा ॥
नत्वा निवेद्य सर्वं तु नृपतिः समुवाच ह ॥ 42 ॥
4.25.m:
At that moment, seeing his guru joyfully arriving there,
having bowed down and reported everything, the king spoke:

4.25.s:
nāyāti muniśārdūlaḥ prayāti dvādaśī tithiḥ ..
saṃkaṭe'sminvidheyaṃ ca vivicya vidhipūrvakam ..
śīghraṃ vada muniśreṣṭha bhadrābhadraṃ ca māmiti .. 43 ..
4.25.d:
नायाति मुनिशार्दूलः प्रयाति द्वादशी तिथिः ॥
संकटेऽस्मिन्विधेयं च विविच्य विधिपूर्वकम् ॥
शीघ्रं वद मुनिश्रेष्ठ भद्राभद्रं च मामिति ॥ 43 ॥
4.25.m:
'The tiger among sages does not arrive, and the Dvādaśī lunar day is slipping away.
Having considered according to rule what ought to be done in this crisis,
tell me quickly, O best of sages, what is auspicious and what is inauspicious.'

4.25.s:
śrutvā nṛpoktiṃ tvaritamuvāca munipuṃgavaḥ ..
hitaṃ tathyaṃ ca vedoktaṃ pariṇāmasukhāvaham .. 44 ..
4.25.d:
श्रुत्वा नृपोक्तिं त्वरितमुवाच मुनिपुंगवः ॥
हितं तथ्यं च वेदोक्तं परिणामसुखावहम् ॥ 44 ॥
4.25.m:
Hearing the king's words, the eminent sage promptly spoke
[words that were] beneficial, truthful, stated in the Vedas, and bringing happiness in their outcome.

4.25.s:
vaśiṣṭha uvāca ..
dvādaśyāṃ samatītāyāṃ trayodaśyāṃ tu pāraṇam ..
upavāsaphalaṃ hatvā vratinaṃ hanti niścitam .. 45 ..
4.25.d:
वशिष्ठ उवाच ॥
द्वादश्यां समतीतायां त्रयोदश्यां तु पारणम् ॥
उपवासफलं हत्वा व्रतिनं हन्ति निश्चितम् ॥ 45 ॥
4.25.m:
When the dvādaśī has passed, breaking the fast on the trayodaśī
destroys the fruit of the fast and surely destroys the performer of the vow.

4.25.s:
brahmahatyāsamaṃ pāpaṃ bhavettasya śrutau śrutam..
bhakṣyadravyaṃ surātulyamityāha kamalodbhavaḥ ..46..
4.25.d:
ब्रह्महत्यासमं पापं भवेत्तस्य श्रुतौ श्रुतम्॥
भक्ष्यद्रव्यं सुरातुल्यमित्याह कमलोद्भवः ॥46॥
4.25.m:
A sin equal to the slaying of a Brahmin would be his, as heard in the Vedas;
the edible substance becomes equal to liquor—thus spoke the Lotus-born [Brahmā].

4.25.s:
na bhojayitvā mūḍhaścedatithiṃ samupasthitam ..
sa trastaḥ kṣudhito bhuṅkte kumbhīpāke vrajeddhuvam..47..
4.25.d:
न भोजयित्वा मूढश्चेदतिथिं समुपस्थितम् ॥
स त्रस्तः क्षुधितो भुङ्क्ते कुम्भीपाके व्रजेद्धुवम्॥47॥
4.25.m:
If a fool, without feeding an unexpected guest who has arrived,
eats, terrified and hungry, he surely goes to Kumbhīpāka.

4.25.s:
śatavarṣaṃ tatra tiṣṭhannaraścāṇḍālatāṃ vrajet ..
vyādhiyukto daridraśca bhavejjanmani janmani .. 48 ..
4.25.d:
शतवर्षं तत्र तिष्ठन्नरश्चाण्डालतां व्रजेत् ॥
व्याधियुक्तो दरिद्रश्च भवेज्जन्मनि जन्मनि ॥ 48 ॥
4.25.m:
Staying there for a hundred years, the man falls into the condition of a Cāṇḍāla,
and afflicted with disease and poor he becomes birth after birth.

4.25.s:
ato'tisūkṣmaṃ kiṃ brūmo'dhunā parama saṃkaṭe ..
rakṣāṃ kuru dvayordharmaṃ samālokya vadāmi te ..49..
4.25.d:
अतोऽतिसूक्ष्मं किं ब्रूमोऽधुना परम संकटे ॥
रक्षां कुरु द्वयोर्धर्मं समालोक्य वदामि ते ॥49॥
4.25.m:
Therefore, what extremely subtle matter shall we declare now in this supreme dilemma?
Protect the duty of both; having considered it, I speak to you:

4.25.s:
upavāsaphalaṃ rakṣa kṛṣṇasya caraṇodakam ..
bhuktvā śīghramapo rājaṃstadbhakṣaṇamabhakṣaṇam ..4.25.50..
4.25.d:
उपवासफलं रक्ष कृष्णस्य चरणोदकम् ॥
भुक्त्वा शीघ्रमपो राजंस्तद्भक्षणमभक्षणम् ॥4.25.50॥
4.25.m:
preserve the fruit of the fast—having quickly consumed the water of Kṛṣṇa’s feet,
the water, O king; that consuming is [both] consuming and non-consuming.

4.25.s:
ityuktvā brahmaṇaḥ putro virarāma mahāmune ..
bubhuje tajjalaṃ kiṃcitkṛṣṇapādāmbujaṃ smaran..51..
4.25.d:
इत्युक्त्वा ब्रह्मणः पुत्रो विरराम महामुने ॥
बुभुजे तज्जलं किंचित्कृष्णपादाम्बुजं स्मरन्॥51॥
4.25.m:
Having spoken thus, the son of Brahmā fell silent, O great sage.
He consumed a little of that water, remembering the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa.

4.25.s:
etasminnantare brahmannājagāma munīśvaraḥ ..
ciccheda kopātsarvajñaḥ svajaṭāṃ nṛpateḥ puraḥ .. 52 ..
4.25.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ब्रह्मन्नाजगाम मुनीश्वरः ॥
चिच्छेद कोपात्सर्वज्ञः स्वजटां नृपतेः पुरः ॥ 52 ॥
4.25.m:
In the meantime, O Brahmin, the lord of sages arrived.
In anger the all-knowing one cut off his matted hair in front of the king.

4.25.s:
tataḥ samutthitaḥ śīghraṃ puruṣo'gniśikhopamaḥ ..
khaḍga hasto mahābhīmo rājendraṃ hantumudyataḥ ..53..
4.25.d:
ततः समुत्थितः शीघ्रं पुरुषोऽग्निशिखोपमः ॥
खड्ग हस्तो महाभीमो राजेन्द्रं हन्तुमुद्यतः ॥53॥
4.25.m:
Then there quickly arose a being resembling a flame of fire,
sword in hand, exceedingly terrible, prepared to slay the best of kings.

4.25.s:
hareścakraṃ ca taṃ dṛṣṭvā sūryakoṭisamaprabham..
ciccheda kṛtyāpuruṣaṃ brāhmaṇaṃ chettumudyatam ..54..
4.25.d:
हरेश्चक्रं च तं दृष्ट्वा सूर्यकोटिसमप्रभम्॥
चिच्छेद कृत्यापुरुषं ब्राह्मणं छेत्तुमुद्यतम् ॥54॥
4.25.m:
And seeing him, Hari's discus, having the radiance of ten million suns,
cut down the figure of destruction and set out to cut down the Brahmin.

4.25.s:
dṛṣṭvā sudarśanaṃ vipro dudrāva bhayavihvalaḥ ..
dvijaḥ paścāttaṃ dadarśa jvaladagniśikhopamam .. 55 ..
4.25.d:
दृष्ट्वा सुदर्शनं विप्रो दुद्राव भयविह्वलः ॥
द्विजः पश्चात्तं ददर्श ज्वलदग्निशिखोपमम् ॥ 55 ॥
4.25.m:
Seeing Sudarśana, the Brahmin fled, overwhelmed with fear;
the twice-born saw it behind him, resembling a blazing flame of fire.

4.25.s:
brahmāṇḍakramaṇaṃ kṛtvā nirviṇṇo'ti bhayākulaḥ ..
taṃ ca matvā jagannāthaṃ brahmāṇaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau .. 56 ..
4.25.d:
ब्रह्माण्डक्रमणं कृत्वा निर्विण्णोऽति भयाकुलः ॥
तं च मत्वा जगन्नाथं ब्रह्माणं शरणं ययौ ॥ 56 ॥
4.25.m:
Having traversed the cosmic egg, despondent, exceedingly agitated by fear,
and regarding Brahmā as the lord of the universe, he went to him for refuge.

4.25.s:
trāhitrāhītyevamuktvā viveśa brahmaṇaḥ sabhām ..
utthāya brahmā viprendraṃ papraccha kuśalaṃ mune .. 57 ..
4.25.d:
त्राहित्राहीत्येवमुक्त्वा विवेश ब्रह्मणः सभाम् ॥
उत्थाय ब्रह्मा विप्रेन्द्रं पप्रच्छ कुशलं मुने ॥ 57 ॥
4.25.m:
Crying out, “Save me! Save me!”, he entered Brahmā’s assembly.
Rising, Brahmā asked the foremost of Brahmins about his welfare, O sage.

4.25.s:
sarvaṃ sa kathayāmāsa vṛttāntaṃ mūlato vidhim ..
śrutvā brahmā niśaśvāsa tamuvāca bhayākulaḥ .. 58 ..
4.25.d:
सर्वं स कथयामास वृत्तान्तं मूलतो विधिम् ॥
श्रुत्वा ब्रह्मा निशश्वास तमुवाच भयाकुलः ॥ 58 ॥
4.25.m:
He told the whole story from its root to the Creator.
Hearing it, Brahmā sighed and, agitated by fear, spoke to him.

4.25.s:
brahmovāca ..
haridāsaṃ vatsa śaptuṃ gato'si kasya tejasā ..
rakṣitā yasya bhagavāṃstaṃ ko hantā jagattraye .. 59 ..
4.25.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ॥
हरिदासं वत्स शप्तुं गतोऽसि कस्य तेजसा ॥
रक्षिता यस्य भगवांस्तं को हन्ता जगत्त्रये ॥ 59 ॥
4.25.m:
Child, by whose power did you go to curse a servant of Hari?
He whose protector is the Lord—who can slay him in the three worlds?

4.25.s:
kṣudrāṇāṃ mahatāṃ caiva bhaktānāṃ rakṣaṇāya ca ..
rarakṣa saṃtataṃ cakraṃ śrīharirbhaktavatsalaḥ .. 4.25.60 ..
4.25.d:
क्षुद्राणां महतां चैव भक्तानां रक्षणाय च ॥
ररक्ष संततं चक्रं श्रीहरिर्भक्तवत्सलः ॥ 4.25.60 ॥
4.25.m:
For the protection of the lowly and of the great devotees alike,
glorious Hari, who is affectionate to his devotees, constantly deployed his discus.

4.25.s:
yo mūḍho vaiṣṇavaṃ dveṣṭi viṣṇuprāṇasamaṃ dvija ..
tasya saṃhārakartāraṃ saṃhartumīśvaro hariḥ ..61..
4.25.d:
यो मूढो वैष्णवं द्वेष्टि विष्णुप्राणसमं द्विज ॥
तस्य संहारकर्तारं संहर्तुमीश्वरो हरिः ॥61॥
4.25.m:
Whatever fool hates a Vaiṣṇava, who is as dear as Viṣṇu's life, O twice-born,
Hari is the Lord capable of destroying the one who undertakes his destruction.

4.25.s:
śīghraṃ sthānāntaraṃ gaccha vatsa trāṇaṃ na vā'dhunā ..
anyathā tvāṃ mayā sārdhaṃ haniṣyati sudarśanam .. 62 ..
4.25.d:
शीघ्रं स्थानान्तरं गच्छ वत्स त्राणं न वाऽधुना ॥
अन्यथा त्वां मया सार्धं हनिष्यति सुदर्शनम् ॥ 62 ॥
4.25.m:
Quickly go to another place, child; there is no rescue now,
otherwise Sudarśana will kill you along with me.

4.25.s:
kiṃ brahmalokaṃ brahmāṇḍaṃ dagdhuṃ śaktaṃ kṣaṇena yat ..
tejasā viṣṇutulyaṃ yatkenānyena nivāryate .. 63 ..
4.25.d:
किं ब्रह्मलोकं ब्रह्माण्डं दग्धुं शक्तं क्षणेन यत् ॥
तेजसा विष्णुतुल्यं यत्केनान्येन निवार्यते ॥ 63 ॥
4.25.m:
What of Brahmaloka? It is capable of burning the cosmic egg in an instant!
Since it is equal to Viṣṇu in splendour, by whom else can it be warded off?

4.25.s:
brahmaṇo vacanaṃ śrutvā tato dudrāva brāhmaṇaḥ ..
trasto jagāma kailāsaṃ śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ bhiyā .. 64 ..
4.25.d:
ब्रह्मणो वचनं श्रुत्वा ततो दुद्राव ब्राह्मणः ॥
त्रस्तो जगाम कैलासं शंकरं शरणं भिया ॥ 64 ॥
4.25.m:
Hearing Brahmā's words, the Brahmin then fled from there;
terrified, out of fear he went to Kailāsa, to Śaṅkara for refuge.

4.25.s:
kṛpānidhāna māṃ rakṣetyuvāca śaṃkaraṃ bhiyā ..
na praccha kuśalaṃ sarvajño brāhmaṇaṃ śivaḥ .. 65 ..
4.25.d:
कृपानिधान मां रक्षेत्युवाच शंकरं भिया ॥
न प्रच्छ कुशलं सर्वज्ञो ब्राह्मणं शिवः ॥ 65 ॥
4.25.m:
“O treasure of compassion, save me!” he said to Śaṅkara in fear.
The all-knowing Śiva did not ask the Brahmin about his welfare;

4.25.s:
uvāca dīnadīneśaḥ saṃhartā jagatāṃ kṣaṇāt ..
sthiro bhava dvijaśreṣṭha madīyaṃ vacanaṃ śṛṇu .. 66 ..
4.25.d:
उवाच दीनदीनेशः संहर्ता जगतां क्षणात् ॥
स्थिरो भव द्विजश्रेष्ठ मदीयं वचनं शृणु ॥ 66 ॥
4.25.m:
the master of the miserable and distressed, who can destroy the worlds in an instant, spoke:
“Be steady, O best of the twice-born! Listen to my words.”

4.25.s:
śaṃkara uvāca ..
pautrastvaṃ jagatāṃ dhāturatreśca tanayo mune ..
vedajñātā'si sarvajña mūrkhatulyaṃ tu karma te .. 67 ..
4.25.d:
शंकर उवाच ॥
पौत्रस्त्वं जगतां धातुरत्रेश्च तनयो मुने ॥
वेदज्ञाताऽसि सर्वज्ञ मूर्खतुल्यं तु कर्म ते ॥ 67 ॥
4.25.m:
You are the grandson of the Creator of the worlds and the son of Atri, O sage;
you are a knower of the Vedas, all-wise, but your deed is equal to that of a fool.

4.25.s:
vedeṣu ca purāṇeṣu setihāseṣu sarvataḥ ..
nirūpito yaḥ sarveśastaṃ na jānāsi mūḍhavat .. 68 ..
4.25.d:
वेदेषु च पुराणेषु सेतिहासेषु सर्वतः ॥
निरूपितो यः सर्वेशस्तं न जानासि मूढवत् ॥ 68 ॥
4.25.m:
In the Vedas, in the Purāṇas, and everywhere throughout the Itihāsas,
the Lord of all has been ascertained; like a fool, you do not know him.

4.25.s:
ahaṃ brahmā ca indraśca ādityā vasavastathā ..
dharmendrau ca surāḥ sarve munīndrā manavastathā ..69..
4.25.d:
अहं ब्रह्मा च इन्द्रश्च आदित्या वसवस्तथा ॥
धर्मेन्द्रौ च सुराः सर्वे मुनीन्द्रा मनवस्तथा ॥69॥
4.25.m:
I, Brahmā, Indra, the Ādityas, and likewise the Vasus,
Dharma and Indra, all the gods, the foremost of sages, and likewise the Manus,

4.25.s:
āvirbhūtāstirobhūtā yasya bhrūbhaṅgalīlayā ..
tasya prāṇādhikaṃ bhaktaṃ haṃsi tvaṃ kasya tejasā .. 4.25.70 ..
4.25.d:
आविर्भूतास्तिरोभूता यस्य भ्रूभङ्गलीलया ॥
तस्य प्राणाधिकं भक्तं हंसि त्वं कस्य तेजसा ॥ 4.25.70 ॥
4.25.m:
are manifested and dissolved by the playful knitting of his brow;
by whose power do you slay his devotee, who is dearer to him than his own life?

4.25.s:
ahaṃ brahmā ca kamalā durgā vāṇī ca rādhikā ..
na hi bhaktātparāḥ premṇā bhaktāśca sarvataḥ priyāḥ ..71..
4.25.d:
अहं ब्रह्मा च कमला दुर्गा वाणी च राधिका ॥
न हि भक्तात्पराः प्रेम्णा भक्ताश्च सर्वतः प्रियाः ॥71॥
4.25.m:
I, Brahmā, Kamalā, Durgā, Vāṇī, and Rādhikā
are not superior to a devotee in love; devotees are beloved above all.

4.25.s:
kṣudrāṃśca mahato bhaktāñchaśvadrakṣati yatnataḥ ..
sarvāntarātmā bhagavāṃścakreṇa duḥsahena ca .. .. 72 ..
4.25.d:
क्षुद्रांश्च महतो भक्ताञ्छश्वद्रक्षति यत्नतः ॥
सर्वान्तरात्मा भगवांश्चक्रेण दुःसहेन च ॥ ॥ 72 ॥
4.25.m:
Constantly and carefully, the lowly and the great devotees alike are protected
by the Lord, the Inner Self of all, with his irresistible discus.

4.25.s:
niyujya cakraṃ durvāryaṃ svātmatulyaṃ ca tejasā ..
tathā'pi na pratītiśca svayaṃ gacchati rakṣitum .. 73 ..
4.25.d:
नियुज्य चक्रं दुर्वार्यं स्वात्मतुल्यं च तेजसा ॥
तथाऽपि न प्रतीतिश्च स्वयं गच्छति रक्षितुम् ॥ 73 ॥
4.25.m:
Having assigned his irresistible discus, which is equal to himself in splendour,
still having no certainty [of their safety], he goes himself to protect [them].

4.25.s:
svakīyaguṇa nāmnāṃ ca śravaṇādatisaṃbhramaḥ ..
bhaktasaṅge bhramatyeva chāyeva satataṃ hariḥ .. 74 ..
4.25.d:
स्वकीयगुण नाम्नां च श्रवणादतिसंभ्रमः ॥
भक्तसङ्गे भ्रमत्येव छायेव सततं हरिः ॥ 74 ॥
4.25.m:
From hearing the praise of His own qualities and names He feels great agitation;
Hari continually wanders in the company of His devotee, like a shadow.

4.25.s:
kāntā prāṇādhikā śaśvanna hi ko'pi tato'dhikaḥ ..
bhaktāndveṣṭi svayaṃ sā cettūrṇaṃ tyajati tāṃ prabhuḥ .. 75 ..
4.25.d:
कान्ता प्राणाधिका शश्वन्न हि कोऽपि ततोऽधिकः ॥
भक्तान्द्वेष्टि स्वयं सा चेत्तूर्णं त्यजति तां प्रभुः ॥ 75 ॥
4.25.m:
His beloved is dearer to Him than life, constantly; none is dearer than she;
yet if she herself hates His devotees, the Lord quickly abandons her.

4.25.s:
sarveṣāṃ ca priyā viprāḥ svaśarīrādapi dvija ..
brāhmaṇebhyaḥ priyā bhaktāḥ prāṇebhyaśca harerapi .. 76 ..
4.25.d:
सर्वेषां च प्रिया विप्राः स्वशरीरादपि द्विज ॥
ब्राह्मणेभ्यः प्रिया भक्ताः प्राणेभ्यश्च हरेरपि ॥ 76 ॥
4.25.m:
Brahmins are dear to all, even dearer than their own bodies, O twice-born;
and devotees are dearer to Hari than brahmins, and even dearer than His own life.

4.25.s:
īśvarasya priyaḥ ko vā'priyaḥ ko vā jagattraye ..
yaḥ śiṣṭastaṃ bhajecchaśvaddhyāyate satataṃ sadā .. 77 ..
4.25.d:
ईश्वरस्य प्रियः को वाऽप्रियः को वा जगत्त्रये ॥
यः शिष्टस्तं भजेच्छश्वद्ध्यायते सततं सदा ॥ 77 ॥
4.25.m:
Who is dear to God, or who is not dear in the three worlds?
Whoever is virtuous—Him He constantly serves and always continuously meditates upon.

4.25.s:
mahati pralaye brahmanbrahmaṇḍaughe jalaplute ..
na tatra nāśo bhaktānāṃ sarveṣāṃ ca bhaviṣyati .. 78 ..
4.25.d:
महति प्रलये ब्रह्मन्ब्रह्मण्डौघे जलप्लुते ॥
न तत्र नाशो भक्तानां सर्वेषां च भविष्यति ॥ 78 ॥
4.25.m:
In the great dissolution, O brahmin, when the multitude of cosmic eggs is flooded with water,
even there, there will be no destruction for any of His devotees.

4.25.s:
bhaja brāhmaṇa govindaṃ smara tasya padāmbujam ..
sarvāpado vinaśyanti śrīhareḥ smaraṇādapi .. 79 ..
4.25.d:
भज ब्राह्मण गोविन्दं स्मर तस्य पदाम्बुजम् ॥
सर्वापदो विनश्यन्ति श्रीहरेः स्मरणादपि ॥ 79 ॥
4.25.m:
Worship Govinda, O brahmin; remember His lotus feet!
All misfortunes perish even from the remembrance of venerable Hari.

4.25.s:
vraja śīghraṃ ca vaikuṇṭhaṃ vaikuṇṭhaḥ śaraṇaṃ tava ..
dāsyatyevābhayaṃ tubhyaṃ karuṇāsāgaro vibhuḥ .. 4.25.80 ..
4.25.d:
व्रज शीघ्रं च वैकुण्ठं वैकुण्ठः शरणं तव ॥
दास्यत्येवाभयं तुभ्यं करुणासागरो विभुः ॥ 4.25.80 ॥
4.25.m:
Go quickly to Vaikuṇṭha; Vaikuṇṭha is your refuge.
The all-pervading Lord, an ocean of compassion, will surely grant you fearlessness."

4.25.s:
etasminnantare vyāptaṃ kailāsaṃ cakratejasā ..
yathā ca sūryakiraṇaiḥ supradīptaṃ mahītalam .. 81 ..
4.25.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे व्याप्तं कैलासं चक्रतेजसा ॥
यथा च सूर्यकिरणैः सुप्रदीप्तं महीतलम् ॥ 81 ॥
4.25.m:
In the meantime, Kailāsa was pervaded by the brilliance of the disc,
just as the surface of the earth is brightly illuminated by the rays of the sun.

4.25.s:
dagdhā jvālākarālaiśca sarve kailāsavāsinaḥ ..
trāhi trāhītyevamuktvā śaṃkaraṃ śaraṇaṃ yayuḥ .. 82 ..
4.25.d:
दग्धा ज्वालाकरालैश्च सर्वे कैलासवासिनः ॥
त्राहि त्राहीत्येवमुक्त्वा शंकरं शरणं ययुः ॥ 82 ॥
4.25.m:
Burned by the terrifying flames, all the dwellers of Kailāsa,
crying out 'Save us! Save us!', went to Śaṅkara for refuge.

4.25.s:
dṛṣṭvā cakraṃ durviṣahaṃ śaṃkaraḥ karuṇānidhiḥ ..
pārvatyā saha saṃprītyā brāhmaṇāyāśiṣaṃ dadau .. 83 ..
4.25.d:
दृष्ट्वा चक्रं दुर्विषहं शंकरः करुणानिधिः ॥
पार्वत्या सह संप्रीत्या ब्राह्मणायाशिषं ददौ ॥ 83 ॥
4.25.m:
Seeing the unbearable disc, Śaṅkara, a treasure-house of compassion,
along with Pārvatī lovingly gave a blessing to the brahmin:

4.25.s:
tejaḥ satyaṃ tapaḥ satyaṃ yadi ceccirasaṃcitam ..
kṛtāparādho bhītaśca dvijo bhavatu vijvaraḥ .. 84 ..
4.25.d:
तेजः सत्यं तपः सत्यं यदि चेच्चिरसंचितम् ॥
कृतापराधो भीतश्च द्विजो भवतु विज्वरः ॥ 84 ॥
4.25.m:
"If our splendour is true, and if our austerity accumulated over a long time is true,
then may this twice-born, though an offender and terrified, become free from fever!"

4.25.s:
pārvatyuvāca ..
yatprabhormama puṇyeṣu brāhmaṇaḥ śaraṇāgataḥ ..
mamāśiṣā mahābhītyā śīghraṃ bhavatu vijvaraḥ .. 85..
4.25.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ॥
यत्प्रभोर्मम पुण्येषु ब्राह्मणः शरणागतः ॥
ममाशिषा महाभीत्या शीघ्रं भवतु विज्वरः ॥ 85॥
4.25.m:
"Since the brahmin has sought refuge in the merits of my lord,
by my blessing may he, who is in great fear, quickly become free from fever!"

4.25.s:
ityevamuktvā kṛpayā virarāma śivā śivaḥ ..
muniḥ praṇamya deveśaṃ vaikuṇṭhaṃ śaraṇaṃ yayau .. 86 ..
4.25.d:
इत्येवमुक्त्वा कृपया विरराम शिवा शिवः ॥
मुनिः प्रणम्य देवेशं वैकुण्ठं शरणं ययौ ॥ 86 ॥
4.25.m:
Having spoken thus with compassion, Śiva and Śivā paused;
the sage bowed to the lord of gods and went to Vaikuṇṭha for refuge.

4.25.s:
gatvā vaikuṇṭhabhavanaṃ manoyāyī munīśvaraḥ ..
dṛṣṭvā sudarśanaṃ paścādviveśāntaḥpuraṃ hareḥ .. 87 ..
4.25.d:
गत्वा वैकुण्ठभवनं मनोयायी मुनीश्वरः ॥
दृष्ट्वा सुदर्शनं पश्चाद्विवेशान्तःपुरं हरेः ॥ 87 ॥
4.25.m:
Going to the abode of Vaikuṇṭha, traveling at the speed of thought, the lord of sages,
seeing Sudarśana behind him, entered the inner chambers of Hari.

4.25.s:
dadarśa śrīhariṃ vipro ratnasiṃhāsanasthitam ..
śaṅkhacakragadāpadmadharaṃ pītāmbaraṃ param .. 88 ..
4.25.d:
ददर्श श्रीहरिं विप्रो रत्नसिंहासनस्थितम् ॥
शङ्खचक्रगदापद्मधरं पीताम्बरं परम् ॥ 88 ॥
4.25.m: The brahmin saw venerable Hari seated upon a jewelled throne,

4.25.s:
śyāmaṃ caturbhujaṃ śāntaṃ lakṣmīkāntaṃ manoharam ..
ratnālaṃkāraśobhāḍhyaṃ ratnamālāvibhūṣitam .. 89 ..
4.25.d:
श्यामं चतुर्भुजं शान्तं लक्ष्मीकान्तं मनोहरम् ॥
रत्नालंकारशोभाढ्यं रत्नमालाविभूषितम् ॥ 89 ॥
4.25.m:
dark, four-armed, tranquil, the beloved of Lakṣmī, enchanting,
rich in the splendour of jewelled ornaments, adorned with a necklace of jewels,

4.25.s:
īṣaddhāsyaprasannāsyaṃ bhaktānugrahakātaram ..
sadratnasāraracitaṃ kirīṭojjvalaśekharam .. 4.25.90 ..
4.25.d:
ईषद्धास्यप्रसन्नास्यं भक्तानुग्रहकातरम् ॥
सद्रत्नसाररचितं किरीटोज्ज्वलशेखरम् ॥ 4.25.90 ॥
4.25.m: His crest radiant with a diadem made of the finest jewels,

4.25.s:
pārṣadapravarendraiśca sevitaṃ śvetacāmaraiḥ ..
padmāsevitapādābja sarasvatyā stutaṃ puraḥ .. 91 ..
4.25.d:
पार्षदप्रवरेन्द्रैश्च सेवितं श्वेतचामरैः ॥
पद्मासेवितपादाब्ज सरस्वत्या स्तुतं पुरः ॥ 91 ॥
4.25.m:
served by the best among His chief attendants with white whisks,
His lotus feet served by Padmā, praised before Him by Sarasvatī,

4.25.s:
sunandanandakumudapracaṇḍādibhirāvṛtam ..
guṇānuvādaṃ gāyantaṃ tantraiḥ paśyantamīpsitam .. 92 ..
4.25.d:
सुनन्दनन्दकुमुदप्रचण्डादिभिरावृतम् ॥
गुणानुवादं गायन्तं तन्त्रैः पश्यन्तमीप्सितम् ॥ 92 ॥
4.25.m:
surrounded by Sunanda, Nanda, Kumuda, Pracaṇḍa, and others,
who were singing the recital of His virtues, looking upon His desired form with stringed instruments.

4.25.s:
evaṃbhūtaṃ prabhuṃ dṛṣṭvā daṇḍavatpraṇanāma ca ..
tuṣṭāva sāmavedoktastotreṇa parameśvaram .. 93 ..
4.25.d:
एवंभूतं प्रभुं दृष्ट्वा दण्डवत्प्रणनाम च ॥
तुष्टाव सामवेदोक्तस्तोत्रेण परमेश्वरम् ॥ 93 ॥
4.25.m: Seeing the Lord who was thus, he bowed down like a rod

4.25.s:
.. durvāsā uvāca .. ..
trāhi māṃ kamalākānta trāhi māṃ karuṇānidhe ..
dīnabandho'tidīneśa karuṇāsāgara prabho .. 94 ..
4.25.d:
॥ दुर्वासा उवाच ॥ ॥
त्राहि मां कमलाकान्त त्राहि मां करुणानिधे ॥
दीनबन्धोऽतिदीनेश करुणासागर प्रभो ॥ 94 ॥
4.25.m:
"Save me, O beloved of Kamalā! Save me, O treasure-house of compassion,
O friend of the wretched, Lord of the exceedingly wretched, O ocean of compassion, O Lord!

4.25.s:
vedavedāṅgasaṃsraṣṭurvidhātuśca svayaṃ vidhe ..
mṛtyormṛtyuḥ kālakāla trāhi māṃ saṃkaṭārṇave .. 95 ..
4.25.d:
वेदवेदाङ्गसंस्रष्टुर्विधातुश्च स्वयं विधे ॥
मृत्योर्मृत्युः कालकाल त्राहि मां संकटार्णवे ॥ 95 ॥
4.25.m:
O Ordainer of the Creator himself, who created the Vedas and the Vedāṅgas,
O Death of death, O Time of time, save me in this ocean of distress!

4.25.s:
saṃhārakartuḥ saṃhāraḥ sarveśaḥ sarvakāraṇaḥ ..
mahāviṣṇutarorbījaṃ rakṣa māṃ bhavasāgare .. 96 ..
4.25.d:
संहारकर्तुः संहारः सर्वेशः सर्वकारणः ॥
महाविष्णुतरोर्बीजं रक्ष मां भवसागरे ॥ 96 ॥
4.25.m:
O Destruction of the destroyer, O Lord of all, O Cause of all,
O Seed of the tree of Mahāviṣṇu, protect me in the ocean of worldly existence!

4.25.s:
śaraṇāgataśokārtabhayatrāṇaparāyaṇa ..
bhagavannava māṃ bhītaṃ nārāyaṇa namo'stu te .. 97 ..
4.25.d:
शरणागतशोकार्तभयत्राणपरायण ॥
भगवन्नव मां भीतं नारायण नमोऽस्तु ते ॥ 97 ॥
4.25.m:
O You who are devoted to delivering those who have sought refuge, the afflicted and the terrified,
O Blessed One, protect me who am frightened; O Nārāyaṇa, homage to You!

4.25.s:
vedeṣvādyaṃ ca yadvastu vedāḥ stotuṃ na ca kṣamāḥ ..
sarasvatī jaḍībhūtā kiṃ stuvanti vipaścitaḥ .. .. 97 ..
4.25.d:
वेदेष्वाद्यं च यद्वस्तु वेदाः स्तोतुं न च क्षमाः ॥
सरस्वती जडीभूता किं स्तुवन्ति विपश्चितः ॥ ॥ 97 ॥
4.25.m:
Even the Vedas are not capable of praising that reality which is first among the Vedas;
when Sarasvatī is rendered dumb, how can the wise praise It?

4.25.s:
śeṣaḥ sahasravaktreṇa yaṃ stotuṃ jaḍatāṃ vrajet ..
pañcavaktro jaḍībhūto jaḍībhūtaścaturmukhaḥ .. 99 ..
4.25.d:
शेषः सहस्रवक्त्रेण यं स्तोतुं जडतां व्रजेत् ॥
पञ्चवक्त्रो जडीभूतो जडीभूतश्चतुर्मुखः ॥ 99 ॥
4.25.m:
He whom Śeṣa with a thousand mouths becomes dumb when trying to praise,
the Five-faced [Śiva] has become dumb, and the Four-faced [Brahmā] has become dumb;

4.25.s:
śrutayaḥ smṛtikartāro vāṇī cetstotumakṣamā ..
ko'haṃ vipraśca vedajñaḥ śiṣyaḥ kiṃ staumi mānada .. 4.25.100 ..
4.25.d:
श्रुतयः स्मृतिकर्तारो वाणी चेत्स्तोतुमक्षमा ॥
कोऽहं विप्रश्च वेदज्ञः शिष्यः किं स्तौमि मानद ॥ 4.25.100 ॥
4.25.m:
if the Śrutis, the authors of the Smṛtis, and Vāṇī are unable to praise,
who am I, a brahmin knowing the Vedas, a mere pupil? How can I praise You, O granter of honour?

4.25.s:
manūnāṃ ca mahendrāṇāmaṣṭāviṃśatime gate ..
divāniśaṃ yasya vidheraṣṭottaraśatāyuṣaḥ .. 101 ..
4.25.d:
मनूनां च महेन्द्राणामष्टाविंशतिमे गते ॥
दिवानिशं यस्य विधेरष्टोत्तरशतायुषः ॥ 101 ॥
4.25.m:
When twenty-eight cycles of Manus and great Indras have passed,
a day and night are completed for Brahmā, whose lifespan is a hundred and eight years;

4.25.s:
tasya pāto bhavedyasya cakṣurunmīlanena ca ..
tamanirvacanīyaṃ ca kiṃ staumi pāhi māṃ prabho .. 102 ..
4.25.d:
तस्य पातो भवेद्यस्य चक्षुरुन्मीलनेन च ॥
तमनिर्वचनीयं च किं स्तौमि पाहि मां प्रभो ॥ 102 ॥
4.25.m:
and his fall occurs with merely the opening of Your eyes!
How can I praise Him who is beyond all description? Protect me, O Lord!"

4.25.s:
ityevaṃ stavanaṃ kṛtvā papāta caraṇāmbuje ..
nayanāmbujanīreṇa siṣeca bhayavihvalaḥ ..103..
4.25.d:
इत्येवं स्तवनं कृत्वा पपात चरणाम्बुजे ॥
नयनाम्बुजनीरेण सिषेच भयविह्वलः ॥103॥
4.25.m:
Having thus offered praise, he fell at his lotus feet;
Overcome with fear, he bathed them with water from his lotus eyes. (103)

4.25.s:
durvāsasā kṛtaṃ stotraṃ hareśca paramātmanaḥ ..
puṇyadaṃ sāmavedoktaṃ jaganmaṅgalanāmakam .. 104 ..
4.25.d:
दुर्वाससा कृतं स्तोत्रं हरेश्च परमात्मनः ॥
पुण्यदं सामवेदोक्तं जगन्मङ्गलनामकम् ॥ 104 ॥
4.25.m:
This hymn of praise composed by Durvāsas to Hari, the Paramātman,
Grants merit, is taught in the Sāmaveda, and is named Jaganmaṅgala. (104)

4.25.s:
yaḥ paṭhetsaṃkaṭagrasto bhaktiyuktaśca saṃyataḥ ..
nārāyaṇastaṃ kṛpayā śīghramāgatya rakṣati .. 105 ..
4.25.d:
यः पठेत्संकटग्रस्तो भक्तियुक्तश्च संयतः ॥
नारायणस्तं कृपया शीघ्रमागत्य रक्षति ॥ 105 ॥
4.25.m:
Whoever, beset by distress, recites it with devotion and self-restraint,
Nārāyaṇa compassionately arrives at once and protects him. (105)

4.25.s:
rājadvāre śmaśāne ca kārāgāre bhayākule ..
śatrugraste dasyubhītau hiṃsrajantusamanvite .. .. 106..
4.25.d:
राजद्वारे श्मशाने च कारागारे भयाकुले ॥
शत्रुग्रस्ते दस्युभीतौ हिंस्रजन्तुसमन्विते ॥ ॥ 106॥
4.25.m:
At the king's gate, in a cremation ground, or in a terrifying prison,
When seized by enemies, in fear of robbers, or surrounded by predatory beasts, (106)

4.25.s:
veṣṭite rājasainyena magne pote mahārṇave..
stotrasmaraṇamātreṇa mucyate nātra saṃśayaḥ .. 107 ..
4.25.d:
वेष्टिते राजसैन्येन मग्ने पोते महार्णवे॥
स्तोत्रस्मरणमात्रेण मुच्यते नात्र संशयः ॥ 107 ॥
4.25.m: Surrounded by the king’s army, or when a boat is sinking in the great ocean,

4.25.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca ..
muneśca stavanaṃ śrutvā bhagavānbhaktavatsalaḥ ..
prahasyovāca madhuraṃ pīyūṣavṛṣṭivanmudā .. 108 ..
4.25.d:
नारायण उवाच ॥
मुनेश्च स्तवनं श्रुत्वा भगवान्भक्तवत्सलः ॥
प्रहस्योवाच मधुरं पीयूषवृष्टिवन्मुदा ॥ 108 ॥
4.25.m:
Having heard the sage's praise, the Blessed One, fond of his devotees,
Smiled and spoke sweetly with joy, like a shower of nectar. (108)

4.25.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
uttiṣṭhottiṣṭha bhadraṃ te bhaviṣyati vareṇa me ..
kiṃ tu me vacanaṃ nityaṃ śṛṇu satyaṃ sukhāvaham .. 109 ..
4.25.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥
उत्तिष्ठोत्तिष्ठ भद्रं ते भविष्यति वरेण मे ॥
किं तु मे वचनं नित्यं शृणु सत्यं सुखावहम् ॥ 109 ॥
4.25.m:
"Arise, arise! Good fortune will be yours through my boon.
Yet hear my eternal word, truthful and bringing happiness: (109)

4.25.s:
anyeṣāṃ ca bhavejjñānaṃ śrutvā śāstraṃ satāṃ mukhāt ..
svamūrtimanti śāstrāṇi bhavetsantaścaranti hi .. 4.25.110 ..
4.25.d:
अन्येषां च भवेज्ज्ञानं श्रुत्वा शास्त्रं सतां मुखात् ॥
स्वमूर्तिमन्ति शास्त्राणि भवेत्सन्तश्चरन्ति हि ॥ 4.25.110 ॥
4.25.m:
Others obtain knowledge by hearing the scripture from the mouths of the virtuous;
Indeed, the virtuous roam as the scriptures embodied in their own form. (110)

4.25.s:
karma vedaviruddhaṃ ca sarveṣāmatigarhitam ..
karoti vidvāṃścejjñātvā sa ca jīvanmṛtādhikaḥ .. 111 ..
4.25.d:
कर्म वेदविरुद्धं च सर्वेषामतिगर्हितम् ॥
करोति विद्वांश्चेज्ज्ञात्वा स च जीवन्मृताधिकः ॥ 111 ॥
4.25.m:
An action opposed to the Veda is utterly condemned for all;
If a learned man knowingly performs it, he is worse than living-dead. (111)

4.25.s:
purāṇeṣu ca vedeṣu cetihāseṣu brāhmaṇa ..
vaiṣṇavānāṃ ca mahimā śrutaḥ sarvaiśca sarvataḥ ..112..
4.25.d:
पुराणेषु च वेदेषु चेतिहासेषु ब्राह्मण ॥
वैष्णवानां च महिमा श्रुतः सर्वैश्च सर्वतः ॥112॥
4.25.m:
In the Purāṇas, the Vedas, and the Itihāsas, O brahmin,
The greatness of the Vaiṣṇavas has been heard everywhere by all. (112)

4.25.s:
ahaṃ prāṇā vaiṣṇavānāṃ mama prāṇāśca vaiṣṇavāḥ ..
tāneva dveṣṭi yo mūḍho mamāsūnāṃ ca hiṃsakaḥ .. 113 ..
4.25.d:
अहं प्राणा वैष्णवानां मम प्राणाश्च वैष्णवाः ॥
तानेव द्वेष्टि यो मूढो ममासूनां च हिंसकः ॥ 113 ॥
4.25.m:
I am the life of the Vaiṣṇavas, and the Vaiṣṇavas are my life;
The fool who hates them is the slayer of my very breath. (113)

4.25.s:
putrānpautrānkalatrāṃśca rājyaṃ lakṣmīṃ vihāya ca ..
dhyāyante satataṃ ye māṃ ko me tebhyaḥ paraḥ priyaḥ .. .. 114 ..
4.25.d:
पुत्रान्पौत्रान्कलत्रांश्च राज्यं लक्ष्मीं विहाय च ॥
ध्यायन्ते सततं ये मां को मे तेभ्यः परः प्रियः ॥ ॥ 114 ॥
4.25.m:
Abandoning sons, grandsons, wives, kingdom, and fortune,
Those who constantly meditate upon me—who is dearer to me than they? (114)

4.25.s:
parā bhaktānna me prāṇā na ca lakṣmīrna śaṅkaraḥ ..
na bhāratī na ca brahmā na durgā na gaṇeśvaraḥ .. 115 ..
4.25.d:
परा भक्तान्न मे प्राणा न च लक्ष्मीर्न शङ्करः ॥
न भारती न च ब्रह्मा न दुर्गा न गणेश्वरः ॥ 115 ॥
4.25.m:
Neither my own life-breath, nor Lakṣmī, nor Śaṅkara is dearer than a devotee;
Neither Bhāratī, nor Brahmā, nor Durgā, nor Gaṇeśvara, (115)

4.25.s:
na brāhmaṇā na vedāśca na vedajananī parā ..
na gopī na ca gopālā na rādhā praṇataḥ priyāḥ ..116..
4.25.d:
न ब्राह्मणा न वेदाश्च न वेदजननी परा ॥
न गोपी न च गोपाला न राधा प्रणतः प्रियाः ॥116॥
4.25.m:
Nor the brahmins, nor the Vedas, nor the supreme Mother of the Vedas,
Nor the gopīs, nor the cowherds, nor Rādhā, are dearer than one bowed [to me] in devotion. (116)

4.25.s:
ityevaṃ kathitaṃ sarvaṃ satyaṃ sāraṃ ca vāstavam ..
na praśaṃsāparaṃ teṣāṃ te ca prāṇādhikāḥ priyāḥ .. 117 ..
4.25.d:
इत्येवं कथितं सर्वं सत्यं सारं च वास्तवम् ॥
न प्रशंसापरं तेषां ते च प्राणाधिकाः प्रियाः ॥ 117 ॥
4.25.m:
Thus all this has been spoken truthfully, essentially, and factually;
It is not merely high praise of them: they are dearer to me than life. (117)

4.25.s:
māṃ dviṣanti ca ye mūḍhā jñānahīnāśca vañcitāḥ ..
ātmānaṃ ye na jānanti te yānti nirayaṃ ciram ..118..
4.25.d:
मां द्विषन्ति च ये मूढा ज्ञानहीनाश्च वञ्चिताः ॥
आत्मानं ये न जानन्ति ते यान्ति निरयं चिरम् ॥118॥
4.25.m:
Those fools who hate me, bereft of knowledge and deceived,
Who do not know the self, go to hell for a long time. (118)

4.25.s:
ye dviṣanti ca madbhaktānprāṇānāmadhikaṃ priyān..
teṣāṃ śāstā tvahaṃ tūrṇaṃ paratra nirayaṃ ciram .. 119 ..
4.25.d:
ये द्विषन्ति च मद्भक्तान्प्राणानामधिकं प्रियान्॥
तेषां शास्ता त्वहं तूर्णं परत्र निरयं चिरम् ॥ 119 ॥
4.25.m:
And those who hate my devotees, who are dearer to me than life,
I am their punisher swiftly, [sending them] to hell for a long time in the hereafter. (119)

4.25.s:
prabhāvo'haṃ ca sarveṣāmīśvaraḥ paripālakaḥ..
na ca vyāpī svatantro'haṃ bhaktādhīno divāniśam..4.25.120..
4.25.d:
प्रभावोऽहं च सर्वेषामीश्वरः परिपालकः॥
न च व्यापी स्वतन्त्रोऽहं भक्ताधीनो दिवानिशम्॥4.25.120॥
4.25.m:
I am the sovereign power, the Lord, and the protector of all;
Yet I am not all-pervasive and independent [here]: day and night I am subservient to my devotee. (120)

4.25.s:
goloke vā'tha vaikuṇṭhe dvibhujaṃ ca caturbhujam ..
rūpamātramidaṃ śaśvatprāṇā me bhaktasannidhau .. 121 ..
4.25.d:
गोलोके वाऽथ वैकुण्ठे द्विभुजं च चतुर्भुजम् ॥
रूपमात्रमिदं शश्वत्प्राणा मे भक्तसन्निधौ ॥ 121 ॥
4.25.m:
Whether in Goloka or in Vaikuṇṭha, two-armed or four-armed,
This is merely my form constantly; my life-breath is in the presence of my devotee. (121)

4.25.s:
yaduktaṃ bhaktadattaṃ ca bhakṣaṇīyaṃ ca tanmama ..
abhakṣyaṃ dravyamanyena dattaṃ cedamṛtopamam .. 122 ..
4.25.d:
यदुक्तं भक्तदत्तं च भक्षणीयं च तन्मम ॥
अभक्ष्यं द्रव्यमन्येन दत्तं चेदमृतोपमम् ॥ 122 ॥
4.25.m:
Whatever has been uttered and given by a devotee is fit for me to eat,
While a substance offered by another is inedible, even if like nectar. (122)

4.25.s:
aṃbarīṣaṃ nṛpaśreṣṭhaṃ nirīhaṃ tamahiṃsakam ..
kathaṃ haṃsi dayāśīlaṃ sarvaprāṇihite ratam .. 123 ..
4.25.d:
अंबरीषं नृपश्रेष्ठं निरीहं तमहिंसकम् ॥
कथं हंसि दयाशीलं सर्वप्राणिहिते रतम् ॥ 123 ॥
4.25.m:
Why do you seek to kill Ambarīṣa, the best of kings, desireless, non-violent,
Compassionate by nature, and devoted to the welfare of all living beings? (123)

4.25.s:
dayāṃ kurvaṃti ye santaḥ satataṃ sarvajantuṣu ..
tāndviṣanti ca ye mūḍhāsteṣāṃ hantā'hameva ca ..124..
4.25.d:
दयां कुर्वंति ये सन्तः सततं सर्वजन्तुषु ॥
तान्द्विषन्ति च ये मूढास्तेषां हन्ताऽहमेव च ॥124॥
4.25.m:
The virtuous who constantly show compassion to all creatures—
Those fools who hate them, I myself am their slayer. (124)

4.25.s:
bhaktānāṃ hiṃsakaṃ śatrumahaṃ rakṣitumakṣamaḥ..
ambarīṣālayaṃ gaccha sa tvāṃ rakṣitumīśvaraḥ .. 125 ..
4.25.d:
भक्तानां हिंसकं शत्रुमहं रक्षितुमक्षमः॥
अम्बरीषालयं गच्छ स त्वां रक्षितुमीश्वरः ॥ 125 ॥
4.25.m:
I am unable to protect an enemy who harms my devotees;
Go to the abode of Ambarīṣa: he is capable of protecting you." (125)

4.25.s:
nārāyaṇa uvāca ..
idaṃ vākyaṃ ca tacchrutvā brāhmaṇo bhayavihvalaḥ ..
viṣaṇṇamānasastasthau smarankṛṣṇapadāmbujam ..126..
4.25.d:
नारायण उवाच ॥
इदं वाक्यं च तच्छ्रुत्वा ब्राह्मणो भयविह्वलः ॥
विषण्णमानसस्तस्थौ स्मरन्कृष्णपदाम्बुजम् ॥126॥
4.25.m:
Hearing this speech, the brahmin, overwhelmed with fear,
Stood with a dejected mind, remembering the lotus feet of Kṛṣṇa. (126)

4.25.s:
etasminnantare brahmā bhavānyā saha śaṃkaraḥ ..
dharmaścendrādayo devā ājagmurmunipuṅgavāḥ... .. 127 ..
4.25.d:
एतस्मिन्नन्तरे ब्रह्मा भवान्या सह शंकरः ॥
धर्मश्चेन्द्रादयो देवा आजग्मुर्मुनिपुङ्गवाः॥॥। 127 ॥
4.25.m:
In the meantime, Brahmā, Śaṅkara together with Bhavānī,
Dharma, the gods headed by Indra, and the foremost sages arrived. (127)

4.25.s:
praṇamya tuṣṭuvuḥ sarve paramātmānamīśvaram ..
pulakāñcitasarvāṅgā bhaktinamrātmakaṃdharāḥ .. 128 ..
4.25.d:
प्रणम्य तुष्टुवुः सर्वे परमात्मानमीश्वरम् ॥
पुलकाञ्चितसर्वाङ्गा भक्तिनम्रात्मकंधराः ॥ 128 ॥
4.25.m:
Having bowed down, they all praised the Paramātman, the Lord,
All their limbs thrilled with horripilation, their necks bent low in devotion. (128)

4.25.s:
brahmovāca ..
svātmasvarūpa nirlipta bhaktānugrahakātara ..
bhaktāparādhajanakaṃ rakṣa brāhmaṇapuṅgavam .. 129 ..
4.25.d:
ब्रह्मोवाच ॥
स्वात्मस्वरूप निर्लिप्त भक्तानुग्रहकातर ॥
भक्तापराधजनकं रक्ष ब्राह्मणपुङ्गवम् ॥ 129 ॥
4.25.m:
"O you whose form is your own self, unattached, anxious to show grace to devotees!
Protect this foremost of brahmins who has committed an offence against a devotee!" (129)

4.25.s:
mahādeva uvāca ..
dīnabandho jagannātha nāyaṃ vipro jagadbahiḥ ..
kṛtāparādhaṃ dīnaṃ ca pāhīmaṃ śaraṇāgatam .. 4.25.130 ..
4.25.d:
महादेव उवाच ॥
दीनबन्धो जगन्नाथ नायं विप्रो जगद्बहिः ॥
कृतापराधं दीनं च पाहीमं शरणागतम् ॥ 4.25.130 ॥
4.25.m:
"O friend of the helpless, O Lord of the universe, this Brahmin is not outside the universe.
Protect this helpless one who has committed an offense and has come [to You] for refuge."

4.25.s:
pārvatyuvāca ..
bhakta evāṃbarīṣaste na dvijā na surā vayam ..
sarveṣāmīśvarastvaṃ ca rakṣa vipraṃ kṛtāgasam .. 131 ..
4.25.d:
पार्वत्युवाच ॥
भक्त एवांबरीषस्ते न द्विजा न सुरा वयम् ॥
सर्वेषामीश्वरस्त्वं च रक्ष विप्रं कृतागसम् ॥ 131 ॥
4.25.m:
"Is Ambarīṣa alone Your devotee, and not the Brahmins, not we gods?
You are the Lord of all; protect the Brahmin who has committed a sin."

4.25.s:
dharma uvāca ..
sarveṣāṃ janakastvaṃ ca pātā daṇḍakṛdīśvaraḥ..
śiśuhetoḥ śiśuṃ hanti pitetyevaṃ kutaḥ prabho .. 132 ..
4.25.d:
धर्म उवाच ॥
सर्वेषां जनकस्त्वं च पाता दण्डकृदीश्वरः॥
शिशुहेतोः शिशुं हन्ति पितेत्येवं कुतः प्रभो ॥ 132 ॥
4.25.m:
"You are the father of all, the protector, the dispenser of punishment, the Lord.
How can a father slay a child for the sake of another child, O Lord?"

4.25.s:
iṃdra uvāca ..
kṛpayā samatā śaśvatsarveṣu jīviṣu prabho ..
aparādhaphalaṃ bhūtamadhunā pātumarhasi .. 133 ..
4.25.d:
इंद्र उवाच ॥
कृपया समता शश्वत्सर्वेषु जीविषु प्रभो ॥
अपराधफलं भूतमधुना पातुमर्हसि ॥ 133 ॥
4.25.m:
"By grace, You have constant impartiality toward all living beings, O Lord.
The fruit of his offense has been experienced; now You ought to protect him."

4.25.s:
rudra uvāca ..
śāntiṃ kartuṃ samucitamucitaṃ sāṃprataṃ kuru ..
kṛtakuṇṭhasya mūlasya pālanaṃ kartumarhasi .. 134 ..
4.25.d:
रुद्र उवाच ॥
शान्तिं कर्तुं समुचितमुचितं सांप्रतं कुरु ॥
कृतकुण्ठस्य मूलस्य पालनं कर्तुमर्हसि ॥ 134 ॥
4.25.m:
"It is appropriate to bring about peace; do now what is fitting.
You ought to protect this foundation that has been blunted."

4.25.s:
dikpāla uvāca ..
kṛtāparādhaṃ vipraṃ ca chettumarhasi na śrutau ..
aparādhaśamaṃ kṛtvā sadā pāti sadīśvaraḥ .. 135 ..
4.25.d:
दिक्पाल उवाच ॥
कृतापराधं विप्रं च छेत्तुमर्हसि न श्रुतौ ॥
अपराधशमं कृत्वा सदा पाति सदीश्वरः ॥ 135 ॥
4.25.m:
"It is not found in the Vedas that You should destroy a Brahmin who has committed an offense.
Calming the offense, a good Lord always protects."

4.25.s:
grahā ūcuḥ ..
yo dveṣṭi vaiṣṇavaṃ mūḍhastaṃ ruṣṭā sarvadevatāḥ ..
pīḍāṃ kurmo vayaṃ śaśvatpaścāttvaṃ pātumarhasi .. 136 ..
4.25.d:
ग्रहा ऊचुः ॥
यो द्वेष्टि वैष्णवं मूढस्तं रुष्टा सर्वदेवताः ॥
पीडां कुर्मो वयं शश्वत्पश्चात्त्वं पातुमर्हसि ॥ 136 ॥
4.25.m:
"All the deities are angry with that fool who hates a Vaiṣṇava.
We continually torment him; afterwards, You ought to protect him."

4.25.s:
munaya ūcuḥ ..
nātha vipre parābhūte sarve jīvanmṛtā vayam ..
daṇḍaṃ vidhātumekasya bhavellajjā svajātiṣu .. 137 ..
4.25.d:
मुनय ऊचुः ॥
नाथ विप्रे पराभूते सर्वे जीवन्मृता वयम् ॥
दण्डं विधातुमेकस्य भवेल्लज्जा स्वजातिषु ॥ 137 ॥
4.25.m:
"O Lord, when a Brahmin is humiliated, we are all as if dead while alive.
To inflict punishment on one brings shame upon his own kind."

4.25.s:
atriruvāca ..
tvayaiva dattaḥ putro me krodhī tvatsevakaḥ sadā ..
na kaṃ bibheti trailokye tejasvī tejasā tava .. 138 ..
4.25.d:
अत्रिरुवाच ॥
त्वयैव दत्तः पुत्रो मे क्रोधी त्वत्सेवकः सदा ॥
न कं बिभेति त्रैलोक्ये तेजस्वी तेजसा तव ॥ 138 ॥
4.25.m:
"My wrathful son was indeed given by You, and he is ever Your servant.
Glorious with Your splendor, he fears no one in the three worlds."

4.25.s:
lakṣmīruvāca ..
kṣamāparādhaṃ bhagavan brāhmaṇaṃ śaraṇāgatam ..
stuvanti deva viprāśca na vipraṃ hantumarhasi .. 139 ..
4.25.d:
लक्ष्मीरुवाच ॥
क्षमापराधं भगवन् ब्राह्मणं शरणागतम् ॥
स्तुवन्ति देव विप्राश्च न विप्रं हन्तुमर्हसि ॥ 139 ॥
4.25.m:
"O Blessed One, forgive the offense of this Brahmin who has taken refuge.
O God, the Brahmins also praise You; You ought not to kill a Brahmin."

4.25.s:
sarasvatyuvāca ..
bodhayiṣyāmi devānāṃ janakaṃ kāmadaṃ śrutim ..
bhagavansvāmī sarveṣāṃ sarvāṃśca pātumarhasi .. 4.25.140 ..
4.25.d:
सरस्वत्युवाच ॥
बोधयिष्यामि देवानां जनकं कामदं श्रुतिम् ॥
भगवन्स्वामी सर्वेषां सर्वांश्च पातुमर्हसि ॥ 4.25.140 ॥
4.25.m:
"I shall remind the progenitor of the gods, the fulfiller of desires, the source of sacred tradition:
O Blessed One, master of all, You ought to protect everyone."

4.25.s:
pārṣadā ūcuḥ ..
bhavataḥ smṛtimātreṇa sarveṣāṃ sarvamaṅgalam ..
bhavetsarvāpado yānti pāhīmaṃ śaraṇāgatam .. 141 ..
4.25.d:
पार्षदा ऊचुः ॥
भवतः स्मृतिमात्रेण सर्वेषां सर्वमङ्गलम् ॥
भवेत्सर्वापदो यान्ति पाहीमं शरणागतम् ॥ 141 ॥
4.25.m:
"By the mere remembrance of You, all auspiciousness belongs to all,
and all misfortunes vanish; protect this one who has taken refuge."

4.25.s:
nartakā ūcuḥ ..
dāridryabhaṃjana vayaṃ bhikṣukāstava saṃtatam ..
bhikṣāṃ naḥ sāṃprataṃ dehi paritrāṇaṃ dvijasya ca .. 142 ..
4.25.d:
नर्तका ऊचुः ॥
दारिद्र्यभंजन वयं भिक्षुकास्तव संततम् ॥
भिक्षां नः सांप्रतं देहि परित्राणं द्विजस्य च ॥ 142 ॥
4.25.m:
"O Destroyer of poverty, we are Your continual beggars.
Give us alms now: the deliverance of the Brahmin."

4.25.s:
eteṣāṃ stavanaṃ śrutvā prabhuḥ śaraṇavatsalaḥ ..
prahasyovāca vacanaṃ sarvasantoṣakāraṇam .. 143 ..
4.25.d:
एतेषां स्तवनं श्रुत्वा प्रभुः शरणवत्सलः ॥
प्रहस्योवाच वचनं सर्वसन्तोषकारणम् ॥ 143 ॥
4.25.m:
Hearing their praise, the Lord, affectionate to those seeking refuge,
smiled and spoke words that brought satisfaction to all.

4.25.s:
śrībhagavānuvāca ..
sarve śṛṇuta madvākyaṃ nītiyuktaṃ sukhāvaham..
viprarakṣāṃ kariṣyāmi yuṣmākamājñayā dhruvam ..144..
4.25.d:
श्रीभगवानुवाच ॥
सर्वे शृणुत मद्वाक्यं नीतियुक्तं सुखावहम्॥
विप्ररक्षां करिष्यामि युष्माकमाज्ञया ध्रुवम् ॥144॥
4.25.m:
"Hear, all of you, my speech endowed with wisdom and conducive to joy.
By your command, I will certainly protect the Brahmin.

4.25.s:
kiṃ tvayaṃ yātu vaikuṇṭhādambarīṣālayaṃ punaḥ ..
karotu pāraṇaṃ tatra rājñaḥ suprītaye muniḥ .. 145 ..
4.25.d:
किं त्वयं यातु वैकुण्ठादम्बरीषालयं पुनः ॥
करोतु पारणं तत्र राज्ञः सुप्रीतये मुनिः ॥ 145 ॥
